item.title: Watch as Nick Sirianni approaches fans, needs guided back to field following win over Cowboys
item.description: Watch as Nick Sirianni approaches fans, needs guided back to field following win over Cowboys originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . At this point, most NFL fans are familiar with Nick Sirianni's style of celebrating. The Eagles head coach has had many moments over the last few years in which he's rubbed opposing fanbases the wrong way by getting a bit too fired up on the sideline, trash-talking with fans and more. So of course, after Philadelphia stunned Dallas on Thanksgiving, Sirianni had something to say about it. In the moments after Joe Milton, Devonta Smith and Jake Elliott led the Eagles to a historic comeback win, Sirianni had to be guided back toward the field by "Big Dom" and more Eagles staffers after celebrating in the area of fans. Here's a look at the viral moment of Sirianni celebrating after the Eagles' win. MORE: How Joe Milton may have secured next contract with performance vs. Cowboys Nick Sirianni approaches fans following Eagles win over Cowboys Not long after Elliott's long-range field goal won it for the Eagles, Sirianni made his way over to an area full of Eagles fans, yelling in their direction and clearly fired up for the comeback. Eagles' chief security officer "Big Dom" was among the staffers who held Sirianni back and attempted to guide him back toward the field so he could go shake hands with Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. #Eagles HC Nick Sirianni ended up by the stands with fans at the end of the game and had to be brought back to the field. https://t.co/3EFV2f6txi — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 Here's another angle of Sirianni approaching fans, which mostly appeared celebratory with Philadelphia fans: Nick Sirianni was fired up after one of the best comebacks in Eagles history against their biggest rival in Dallas https://t.co/PgDTrsRio4 — John Clark (@JClarkNBCS) November 27, 2026 Sirianni also yelled "That's how you fight" as he walked back to the locker room: Nick Sirianni fired up after that win. https://t.co/fAbwKLZo70 — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) November 27, 2026 While the head coach didn't appear to violate any NFL protocols, it was the latest viral exchange in a growing history of Sirianni's personal exchanges with fans, heated moments with players and more. Earlier in the game, he was seen in a back-and-forth with backup running back Will Shipley — though the Eagles certainly put it in the past as they grabbed a win over a division rival. MORE NFL: Updated NFL playoff picture Eagles complete biggest comeback in Thanksgiving history vs. Cowboys Which NFL teams always play on Thanksgiving?

item.title: AEW Collision Thanksgiving Results & Highlights: Trios Championship on the line (11/26/2026)
item.description: AEW AEW is back with a special Thanksgiving night edition of Collision. The show was taped last night at the Liberty First Credit Union Arena in Omaha, Nebraska, and will air tonight at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT on TNT and HBO Max. The November 26 episode of Collision will feature two Blue League matches and one Gold League match in the Continental Classic. Elsewhere on the card, The Dangerous New Level will defend the AEW World Trios Championship against Hechicero, Josh Alexander, and Rocky Romero of the Don Callis Family. TBS Champion Queen Aminata will team up with Mina Shirakawa to take on ROH Women’s World Champion Athena and Billie Starkz in a tag team match. Meanwhile, AEW National Champion Ilja Dragunov will respond to Don Callis’ lucrative offer, while the Kasper Brothers and the Sisters of Sins will also be in action. Below you can find the full match card as well as the show’s results and highlights. Officially announced match card for Collision AEW World Trios Championship Match: The Dangerous New Level ( Swerve Strickland , Austin Creed and Kofi) (c) def. Don Callis Family’s Hechicero, Josh Alexander & Rocky Romero by pinfall Sisters of Sin (Julia Hart & Skye Blue) def. Anna Ray & Nixi XS (enhancement talent) by pinfall Continental Classic Blue League Match: The Demand’s Ricochet def. Brody King by pinfall Continental Classic Blue League Match: “The Alpha” Konosuke Takeshita vs. ROH World Champion Bandido 20-minute time-limit draw Kasper Brothers (Jacob Kasper & Drew Kasper) def. Atlas Armstrong & Talon Graves (enhancement talent) by pinfall ROH Women’s World Champion Athena & Billie Starkz def. TBS Champion Queen Aminata & Mina Shirakawa Continental Classic Gold League Match: “Psycho Killer” Tommaso Ciampa vs. “The Prodigy” Nick Wayne AEW Collision Results and Highlights Related Headlines Will Ospreay Brutally Trolls MJF Following AEW Dynamite Promo California’s Top High School Basketball Forwards, Centers to Watch in 2026-27 California’s Top High School Basketball Guards to Watch in 2026-27 Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: ‘She’s The Reason’ – How Anastasia Nikolakakos’ Twin Sister Helped Fuel Her ONE World Title Dream At ONE SAMURAI 6
item.description: Undefeated Canadian MMA sensation Anastasia “Anniemale” Nikolakakos has spent most of her life chasing martial arts greatness, yet she knows the biggest opportunity of her career would never have materialized without one very special person. On Wednesday, December 2, the 37-year-old battles Japanese wrestling standout Chihiro Sawada for the vacant ONE Women’s Atomweight MMA World Title at ONE SAMURAI 6 inside Yokohama Buntai in Yokohama, Japan. The event streams live to a global audience on live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram The Toronto native carries a flawless 7-0 professional record, highlighted by victories over Vick Souza and Jihin “Shadow Cat” Radzuan in her first two appearances inside the Circle. Those triumphs have placed the former Pallas Athena WFC Atomweight Champion within touching distance of the ultimate prize. Behind her rapid ascent lies an extraordinary family story. Raised in a household where martial arts were a way of life, Nikolakakos once shared Olympic wrestling dreams with her twin sister, Alex, who ultimately set aside her own ambitions to fund and support her sibling’s fighting career. Now, as the Gracie Humaita Bolton representative prepares to compete for 26 pounds of gold, she reflects on the family that shaped her, her complicated relationship with fighting, and the sister who made this moment possible. Growing Up In A Martial Arts Family Long before Nikolakakos ever stepped into a professional MMA bout, martial arts were woven into the fabric of her childhood. Born into a Greek-Italian family in Toronto, the youngest of five children grew up in a lively household constantly packed with siblings, relatives, and friends. Life was rarely quiet, but the nonstop energy created an environment brimming with warmth and excitement. The Canadian recalled: “I’m the youngest of five. I have a twin sister. So it was crazy growing up with a big family. Always people over, always family, always friends. Crazy, loving family, but also crazy.” Photo credit: ONE Championship Her father played a pivotal role in introducing the family to combat sports. A practitioner of Kenpo karate and grappling, he operated two karate studios, immersing Anastasia and her siblings in martial arts from an early age. While the future MMA star also played soccer and basketball, the dojo remained the centerpiece of her upbringing. Even her birthday celebrations were held on the mats at her father’s facilities. She told onefc.com: “My dad owns like two karate studios. On Wednesday, December 2, the 37-year-old battles Japanese wrestling standout Chihiro Sawada for the vacant ONE Women’s Atomweight MMA World Title at ONE SAMURAI 6 inside Yokohama Buntai in Yokohama, Japan. The event streams live to a global audience on live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram The Toronto native carries a flawless 7-0 professional record, highlighted by victories over Vick Souza and Jihin “Shadow Cat” Radzuan in her first two appearances inside the Circle. Those triumphs have placed the former Pallas Athena WFC Atomweight Champion within touching distance of the ultimate prize. Behind her rapid ascent lies an extraordinary family story. Raised in a household where martial arts were a way of life, Nikolakakos once shared Olympic wrestling dreams with her twin sister, Alex, who ultimately set aside her own ambitions to fund and support her sibling’s fighting career. Now, as the Gracie Humaita Bolton representative prepares to compete for 26 pounds of gold, she reflects on the family that shaped her, her complicated relationship with fighting, and the sister who made this moment possible. Growing Up In A Martial Arts Family Long before Nikolakakos ever stepped into a professional MMA bout, martial arts were woven into the fabric of her childhood. Born into a Greek-Italian family in Toronto, the youngest of five children grew up in a lively household constantly packed with siblings, relatives, and friends. Life was rarely quiet, but the nonstop energy created an environment brimming with warmth and excitement. The Canadian recalled: “I’m the youngest of five. I have a twin sister. So it was crazy growing up with a big family. Always people over, always family, always friends. Crazy, loving family, but also crazy.” Photo credit: ONE Championship Her father played a pivotal role in introducing the family to combat sports. A practitioner of Kenpo karate and grappling, he operated two karate studios, immersing Anastasia and her siblings in martial arts from an early age. While the future MMA star also played soccer and basketball, the dojo remained the centerpiece of her upbringing. Even her birthday celebrations were held on the mats at her father’s facilities. She told onefc.com: “My dad owns like two karate studios. So we grew up, my birthday parties were always in the dojo.” View this post on Instagram The Twin Sister Who Put Her Dreams On Hold Although martial arts were a family affair, Nikolakakos forged an unbreakable bond with her twin sister, Alex. The pair grew up training side by side, sharing an ambitious goal of representing Canada in wrestling at the Olympic Games. Anastasia went on to earn podium finishes at the Ontario Federation of School Athletic Associations championships in 2007 and 2008. She recalled their early aspirations: “Before fighting, we wanted to be like on the Olympic team for wrestling. So that was our aspirations, to be on the Olympic team for Canada.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Over time, their paths naturally diverged. Nikolakakos expanded her skill set into Muay Thai, Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, and boxing after a close friend introduced her to other disciplines. During her amateur run, coaches Ryan Grant and Almaz handed her a contract that marked another major milestone in her evolution. Alex, meanwhile, stepped away from wrestling to pursue financial stability. However, she never abandoned her sister’s dream. Instead, she became Anastasia’s staunchest supporter, stepping in with the financial backing that allowed the future MMA standout to keep chasing her goals. For Nikolakakos, the chance to become a ONE World Champion carries profound meaning because of everything her twin sacrificed to get her here. She revealed: “She kind of stopped, I guess, her dream and put everything into me at that time. Really, truly. For a long time she was like my bank account. Honestly, Alex, I love you, twin. She’s the reason, a big part of why I continued. “She kind of put her dreams on hold for me. That’s the truth. And I just, I would love to win for her.” View this post on Instagram The Discipline Behind Nikolakakos’ Unbeaten MMA Career Nikolakakos’ transition from wrestling to MMA quickly yielded championship results. She captured a Canadian amateur MMA title in 2016 before claiming the Pallas Athena WFC Atomweight Championship in 2022. Her spotless professional run eventually earned her a call from ONE Championship, where she announced her arrival with a first-round ground-and-pound knockout of Vick Souza in March 2026. Four months later, she edged Malaysian veteran Jihin Radzuan via split decision to keep her unbeaten streak intact. Beneath those accomplishments lies an intense devotion to her craft, though Nikolakakos draws a sharp line between her love for martial arts and the unforgiving nature of professional competition. She admitted: “I love winning, I love, it’s the best feeling in the world. I hate fighting. I love my training, I love being a martial artist. I’m born for it. I’m born for it, but it’s weird because I hate it at the same time.” View this post on Instagram That contradiction makes more sense when looking at her personality outside the Circle. Away from fight week, Nikolakakos loves dancing, acting, spending time with friends, and entertaining her social media followers. Once a training camp begins, however, a much more serious persona takes over. The Canadian becomes fiercely protective of her focus, often limiting outside contact and trusting her coaches to handle the film study on her opponents. She explained: “I love training. This is my breath, this is my food, this is my life, since from a little girl. So that I love, of course. It’s just the person that I have to become during my camps. I have to be different. “And I like to joke, I like to have fun with my friends, I love dancing, I love acting, I love the social media aspect, but when it comes to fighting, it’s like no joke to me.” View this post on Instagram Source

item.title: Five Levski fans taken to hospital as presidents condemn Marseille violence
item.description: Marseille police said 11 people were injured in the clashes, all of them Bulgarian (Justine MEDDAH) Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence ahead of the Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, with the French and Bulgarian presidents blaming the home fans. The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned "in the strongest possible terms... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans", the Élysée Palace said. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said it was "unacceptable" and "shocking". "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she said in a statement on Facebook. "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety." Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that "these acts would not go unpunished", the Élysée said. Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski fans were gathered. Fighting broke out, with several Marseille fans wearing face coverings, an AFP journalist at the scene said. - 'Violent times' - "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Iotova said: "The French authorities must clarify the circumstances surrounding the attacks and look for responsibility from those who committed them, and UEFA should check how the safety of the Bulgarian fans at the stadium was ensured. "We are ready to provide the necessary assistance to our compatriots. This behaviour is unacceptable!" Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski coach Julio Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Génésio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf/cms/pst

item.title: Eagles Security Forced to Step In as Nick Sirianni Appears to Confront Cowboys Fans After Historic Thanksgiving Win
item.description: Nick Sirianni ©IMAGO/Newscom World The Philadelphia Eagles seem to have finally caught a break this season. With a thrilling end to the Dallas Cowboys game on Thursday, head coach Nick Sirianni has plenty of reasons to celebrate. However, he might have gotten a bit too excited. As seen in the clips , doing rounds on social media, Sirianni is captured heading straight towards the Dallas fans with an agitated look after the win. Philadelphia’s chief security officer Domenico DiSandro, aka Big Dom, rushed to the scene to pull the head coach away from the crowd. Sirianni tried to charge back in. The heated rivalry between the two sides had the heat turned up with Sirianni celebrating the victory right in front of the home crowd. The Eagles head coach was so amped up after the win that he only gave a side hug to Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer, as part of the customary gesture after games. He didn’t even spare the losing coach a second glance and walked away right after. When a head coach's emotions boil over on the biggest stage, it reveals the intensity behind a dominant performance. Stay subscribed for the untold stories shaping the NFL's fiercest rivalries. What initially looked like a comfortable Cowboys victory turned into a stunning Eagles comeback, with Dallas surrendering a 31-10 lead before falling 39-38. Jake Elliott delivered the decisive blow with a 59-yard field goal with just two seconds remaining. The 21-point comeback was the largest ever in Thanksgiving game history for the NFL. The comeback was also made possible by an outstanding performance from Joe Milton, who delivered the best outing of his career. The Eagles quarterback threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing score. In the fourth quarter alone, Philadelphia added 22 points. Dallas tried to stay in the fight with a crazy touchdown from Dak Prescott, who was briefly in the air but managed to hang on to the ball for the score. However, it was all in vain, as Brandon Aubrey missed a field goal later on. This is not the first time that Big Dom had to step up and calm Sirianni down. Back in 2024, the Eagles head coach got into a heated fight with Washington Commanders tight end Zach Ertz as they shook hands after the game. Even though the Eagles wrote one of the best comeback wins on Thanksgiving, the head coach’s reaction did not sit well with many. “Nick Sirianni is classless and should not be an NFL head coach,” Dr. Jeff Mueller wrote on X. “Buddy needs a nap and an ice cream sandwich to go chill out.” Walking back into the stadium after the game, that energy was still present in Sirianni. “We know how to fight,” he can be heard saying as he walks past the media. He also celebrated with Eagles fans nearby before he walked back in, high-fiving them. It all came about in a matter of minutes for Philadelphia, who were on a seven-game losing streak not long ago. Sirianni has reason to celebrate, but he sure will be asked about his behavior with the fans

item.title: Tom Brady rips into Aaron Rodgers for breaking ‘the sanctity of an NFL locker room’
item.description: Another Hall of Fame quarterback is coming out against Aaron Rodgers’ recent comments. This time it was Tom Brady, who kept it professional but made clear that Rodgers’ takedown of the Steelers after his benching needed to stay in house. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place,” Brady said on the Fox broadcast of the Eagles’ 39-38 win over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving in Dallas. “We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. Shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” Fox Sports broadcast analyst Tom Brady looks on before the 49ers’ win over the Cowboys on Nov. 15, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers announced on Tuesday night that they were benching Rodgers against the Broncos in favor of Mason Rudolph, and Rodgers responded on Wednesday by going scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Among Rodgers’ gripes was the 19-year coach falling asleep in team meetings and leading a “1, 2, 3, Packers” chant after a huddle. The Steelers cut Rodgers soon after the appearance on “McAfee,” and he cleared waivers Thursday to become a free agent. Brady, who knows a thing or two about working with longtime coaches, acknowledged that feuds can happen in the locker room, but that doesn’t mean things need to boil over like they did in Pittsburgh. “I wasn’t a perfect player, [Bill Belichick] wasn’t a perfect coach, but we did some things in the game that we’re so proud of now,” Brady said. “And even me being four years removed from the game, things that matter more than winning a Super Bowl or trophy is my relationship with my teammates, my coaches. That’s going to transcend anything you do on the field. “It’s just unfortunate. I hate it, I hate to be even talking about it. It’s a privilege to be in the NFL. You want to inspire the next generation of athletes, and you always want to do it the right way.” Aaron Rodgers wears a frustrated expression during the Steelers’ loss to the Eagles on Nov. 22, 2026, in Philadelphia. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brady wasn’t the only NFL legend who had something to say Thursday on Fox. Michael Strahan, Howie Long, and former Steelers quarterback Terry Bradshaw took time out of the pregame show to discuss Rodgers’ comments. While Rodgers now has the ability to sign with any team, his release by the Steelers may spell the end of his NFL career. ESPN insider Adam Schefter reported Thursday that it’s unlikely Rodgers finds a landing spot to finish out the season.

item.title: Leila Pereira makes curious vow if Palmeiras win the title; watch 🎥
item.description: Leila Pereira makes curious vow if Palmeiras win the title; watch 🎥 Palmeiras president Leila Pereira made an unusual promise should Palmeiras win the Libertadores this year. During an interview on a club podcast, she revealed she is a fan of Brazilian funk and said she would "drop it low" if they beat Estudiantes. Leila said she had originally made the promise at an event at the club's social facilities. See the president's comments below: I'm a classy woman, but that has nothing to do with it...you know what kind of music I love? You won't believe it: I love funk. I love it. I'm going to drop it all the way to the floor. I'll do anything for Palmeiras to win the Libertadores, even dance to funk. I'm going to practice But I like family-friendly funk, okay? Not those funk songs with swear words. That's ugly. I like the beat, I love it. So...if Palmeiras win the Libertadores, you'll get a performance by the Palmeiras president dancing to family-friendly funk because I'm a well-mannered woman Leila Pereira, Palmeiras president The match that will determine whether she has to keep her promise takes place on Saturday (28) at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo. Palmeiras will be chasing their fourth Libertadores title in club history and their first under Leila Pereira's leadership. She was elected club president a week before their third title, won in 2021, but had not yet taken office when the final against Flamengo was played. " This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles
item.description: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jerry Jones is more accessible than most NFL owners, to the point that he reliably speaks with the media after each game. For Cowboys fans, that's a blessing and a curse; they get to hear an immediate response from the owner, but the words aren't always what they want to hear. After Dallas inexplicably blew a 21-point lead to the division-rival Eagles on Thursday, Jones was blunt about the shocking defeat but didn't offer much in the way of potential changes. Here's a look at what Jones had to say. MORE: Joe Milton likely secured NFL future with win over Cowboys Jerry Jones responds to Cowboys' collapse Jones called the loss to the Eagles "numbing" but said he "wouldn't anticipate" coaching changes despite the long layoff before the Cowboys' next game. "We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes at this time," Jones said. That came with a caveat, though. Jones said "nothing we've seen out here tonight" gives him confidence in coach Brian Schottenheimer, but he added, "You've got to look at everything," noting that there are "several more games to go." Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says that “nothing we saw out there tonight” gives him confidence in Brian Schottenheimer, but he reiterates that a change is not on his mind right now. https://t.co/BipwLyTsE9 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 27, 2026 As for the game itself, Jones was clear that everyone on the team, from himself to the players, shared responsibility. "It was ours to take, and we didn't," Jones said. "You have to question everything." QB Dak Prescott agreed with Jones' assessment of the loss. Told that Jones called the defeat "numbing," Prescott told reporters, "That's a good description for how I'm feeling right now." The Cowboys have yet to win back-to-back games this season, and they now trail the Giants by four games in the loss column. Jones typically resists coaching changes as long as possible, but the questions surrounding Schottenheimer aren't likely to fade anytime soon after a Thanksgiving collapse. item.title: Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. injury upgrade is good news for pivotal Raiders clash
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. injury upgrade is good news for pivotal Raiders clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns received an encouraging update on Harold Fannin Jr. ahead of their Sunday Night Football showdown with the Las Vegas Raiders. Fannin, who is dealing with a groin injury, was listed as a full participant on Thursday’s injury report after being limited on Wednesday. There is a catch, though. The Browns only held a walkthrough on Thursday, so the participation levels were estimates, according to Scott Petrak. Still, the upgrade is a positive sign for Cleveland’s top pass-catching threat. It’s also not the first time the groin issue has popped up for Fannin. He was limited with the same injury earlier this month heading into the Browns’ Week 9 matchup with the New Orleans Saints. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He suited up in that game and nearly delivered a memorable win. In the closing minute of overtime, Fannin hauled in a pass, broke two tackles and raced into the end zone. Cleveland’s two-point try failed, however, and the Saints escaped with a 23-22 victory . The second-year tight end has been a reliable weapon this season . He entered the Browns’ Week 10 matchup with the Houston Texans with 453 receiving yards and four touchdowns, and he followed it up with another impactful outing in Cleveland’s 27-24 win. His availability is especially important given what’s at stake. The Browns sit at 6-4 and are fresh off their bye week, putting them right in the thick of the AFC playoff race. A win over the 4-7 Raiders at home would keep them in the hunt in a crowded AFC North . Fannin wasn’t the only tight end to get good news. Blake Whiteheart was also upgraded from limited to full with a hip injury, while rookie guard Austin Barber went from not practicing to limited with a knee issue. On the other hand, defensive ends Derek Barnett and Isaiah McGuire, along with rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston, did not participate for a second straight day. Cleveland’s final injury report is due on Friday. item.title: Bears’ Jeffery Simmons calls out Lions for ‘crying’ over Juice Scruggs’ false starts
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Bears’ Jeffery Simmons calls out Lions for ‘crying’ over Juice Scruggs’ false starts appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Just when the Detroit Lions appeared to have the showdown wrapped up, the Chicago Bears pulled off a wild comeback to secure the victory, 39-35, on Rome Odunze’s six-yard touchdown with three seconds remaining on Thanksgiving Day. The Bears stunned the Lions at Ford Field , erasing an 11-point deficit in the fourth quarter for their sixth straight win and solo possession of the top spot in the NFC North. Plenty of gamesmanship happened, including Jeffery Simmons causing Juice Scruggs to commit a false start three times. When asked about it, Simmons stressed that it was not illegal . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s a lot of crying on that side of the ball when that happened,” said the three-time All-Pro in the video posted by CHGO Bears. “When Jared (Goff) checked, I said, ‘It’s a run.’ It’s not my fault that your center jumped. That’s literally the only time I said something. All the other ones, I think he just knew when I was lined up to the right of his head. That’s on him. He tried to get into position so he could block me, just like the one he fumbled. He saw me, and I’m firing off the ball, but at the end of the day, I don’t have to cheat.” Jeffery Simmons on Lions C Juice Scruggs’ multiple false starts during Thanksgiving matchup: pic.twitter.com/wfRYS3zwOn — CHGO Bears (@CHGO_Bears) November 26, 2026 The 27-year-old Simmons logged three tackles. Chicago improved to 9-2, including 4-1 on the road. “You’re gonna get a lot of complaining when you lose a football game, when you get a false start. But it is what it is,” added the four-time Pro Bowler. He has yet to lose with the Bears since being acquired in a trade with the Tennessee Titans in exchange for draft capital in October. The Bears will host the Jacksonville Jaguars on December 6. item.title: Jared Goff Addresses Chicago Bears Snap-Count Controversy
item.description: Following the Detroit Lions’ heartbreaking 39-35 Thanksgiving Day loss to the Chicago Bears, much of the conversation centered around allegations that Chicago’s defensive players were attempting to simulate Detroit’s offensive snap count. Lions quarterback Jared Goff addressed the situation during his postgame press conference, specifically discussing the actions of Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Although Goff acknowledged that one particular instance stood out to him, the veteran quarterback stopped short of accusing Simmons of intentionally breaking the rules. He also made it abundantly clear that the controversy should not overshadow Detroit’s inability to close out the game. Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) throws a pass during the second half of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jared Goff Addresses Jeffery Simmons’ Actions Goff’s comments came on the same day that Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany accused the Bears of simulating Detroit’s snap count and suggested that the NFL could investigate audio recordings from the game. Goff took a more measured approach, acknowledging how difficult it can be for officials to determine a defensive player’s intentions. “I only think he did it really once that was really egregious to me, where they yell,” Goff said. “It’s a really hard thing to officiate because at what point is he simulating the snap count? At what point is he just talking to his guys? “I understand it happens all across the league. It isn’t the first time it’s happened. “But I’m just trying to make sure that they know that I’m not allowed to simulate snap count with my hands. He shouldn’t be allowed to do it with his voice. “That wasn’t the difference in the game, but that was early, and I don’t believe it happened more than once or twice.” As reported by the Detroit Free Press via Yahoo Sports , Simmons denied mimicking Detroit’s snap count following the game. Goff’s comments suggest that while he was frustrated by what occurred, he recognizes there is a fine line between defensive communication and intentionally disrupting offensive signals. Jared Goff Does Not Want Controversy Overblown Later in his press conference, Goff returned to the subject and reiterated that the alleged snap-count simulation was not responsible for Detroit’s Thanksgiving Day loss. Instead, he placed the responsibility on himself and his teammates to handle those situations better. “I don’t think that should be overblown. I think it happened a couple times, and the officials talked to them,” Goff said. “If they were trying to simulate the snap count or if they weren’t, I don’t know. They could probably say they aren’t, and it’s impossible to officiate, and they’ll never throw a flag on it. “This isn’t the first game that’s happened. item.content:encoded: Following the Detroit Lions’ heartbreaking 39-35 Thanksgiving Day loss to the Chicago Bears, much of the conversation centered around allegations that Chicago’s defensive players were attempting to simulate Detroit’s offensive snap count. Lions quarterback Jared Goff addressed the situation during his postgame press conference, specifically discussing the actions of Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Although Goff acknowledged that one particular instance stood out to him, the veteran quarterback stopped short of accusing Simmons of intentionally breaking the rules. He also made it abundantly clear that the controversy should not overshadow Detroit’s inability to close out the game. Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) throws a pass during the second half of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jared Goff Addresses Jeffery Simmons’ Actions Goff’s comments came on the same day that Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany accused the Bears of simulating Detroit’s snap count and suggested that the NFL could investigate audio recordings from the game. Goff took a more measured approach, acknowledging how difficult it can be for officials to determine a defensive player’s intentions. “I only think he did it really once that was really egregious to me, where they yell,” Goff said. “It’s a really hard thing to officiate because at what point is he simulating the snap count? At what point is he just talking to his guys? “I understand it happens all across the league. It isn’t the first time it’s happened. “But I’m just trying to make sure that they know that I’m not allowed to simulate snap count with my hands. He shouldn’t be allowed to do it with his voice. “That wasn’t the difference in the game, but that was early, and I don’t believe it happened more than once or twice.” As reported by the Detroit Free Press via Yahoo Sports , Simmons denied mimicking Detroit’s snap count following the game. Goff’s comments suggest that while he was frustrated by what occurred, he recognizes there is a fine line between defensive communication and intentionally disrupting offensive signals. Jared Goff Does Not Want Controversy Overblown Later in his press conference, Goff returned to the subject and reiterated that the alleged snap-count simulation was not responsible for Detroit’s Thanksgiving Day loss. Instead, he placed the responsibility on himself and his teammates to handle those situations better. “I don’t think that should be overblown. I think it happened a couple times, and the officials talked to them,” Goff said. “If they were trying to simulate the snap count or if they weren’t, I don’t know. They could probably say they aren’t, and it’s impossible to officiate, and they’ll never throw a flag on it. “This isn’t the first game that’s happened. We’ve got to be able to handle that a little bit better than we did.” Goff’s response is consistent with what Dan Campbell recently revealed about his quarterback’s resilience and competitive mentality . Rather than pointing fingers following a frustrating loss, Goff acknowledged that Detroit needs to be better prepared to handle those situations. Detroit Lions Had Opportunities to Put Bears Away While the snap-count controversy will understandably generate plenty of discussion, the Lions had more than enough opportunities to win Thursday’s game. According to the official Lions game recap , Detroit held a 35-24 fourth-quarter lead before allowing Chicago to score 15 unanswered points. Instead of extending their winning streak to seven games and reversing a historical trend dating back to 1934 , the Lions fell to 8-3 and surrendered first place in the NFC North to the Bears. Whether the NFL eventually examines the allegations raised by Mahogany remains to be seen. As for Goff, his message was clear: Regardless of what Simmons was doing at the line of scrimmage, the Lions had opportunities to win the game and failed to capitalize on them.

item.title: ‘Is This How You Want To Go Out?’ — Russell Wilson Makes Feelings Clear on Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Steelers Exit After Feud With Mike McCarthy
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers turned the Pittsburgh Steelers’ world upside down on Wednesday, airing a ton of dirty laundry regarding his relationship with head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh sided with McCarthy by releasing Rodgers on Wednesday. This situation is still working itself out, with Rodgers clearing waivers, and much is being said about how the abrupt parting of ways has somewhat overshadowed the Thanksgiving slate of games. Many of Rodgers’ peers jumped into the conversation on Wednesday, and that trend continued on Thursday, with Russell Wilson also stepping into the discussion. Russell Wilson Criticizes Aaron Rodgers Over Steelers Fallout Seattle Seahawks legend Russell Wilson was on CBS’ pregame coverage of the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears game on Thursday. During that program, Wilson provided his thoughts on Rodgers and his messy situation with the Steelers. “We’ve all been in the room. Like, we’ve seen coaches fall asleep in moments, long days, long hours. We’ve seen players fall asleep in moments…. The reality is Aaron Rodgers wanted to call the plays, right? And that’s the difference here…. The reality is the ultimatum was the ultimatum,” Wilson said . “If not, I want my release, essentially. And so they made that decision…. It’s about Aaron Rodgers’ legacy…. If I’m his family members, if I’m somebody close to him, I’m his significant other, whatever it may be: ‘Is this how you want to go out?’ After all the success he’s had, is this how you want to go out?… This is a disappointment,” Wilson added. Rodgers played for the Steelers last season prior to McCarthy’s hiring. The future Hall of Fame quarterback mentioned on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday that he vouched for McCarthy to be interviewed for the Pittsburgh job following the 2025 campaign. It was a bit of a mystery as to whether Rodgers would return for 2026. However, he elected to give it one final go and signed a one-year contract to return to Pittsburgh. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator At the start, it seemed things were going well. The Steelers got off to a 6-2 start, and Rodgers was keeping his head above water. Pittsburgh was winning games, at the very least, and was in the running in the AFC North. However, Pittsburgh has lost its last two games. As a result, the team felt like it needed to spark a change somehow, opting to bench Rodgers and start Mason Rudolph in Week 12 against the Denver Broncos. Things went off the rails when Rodgers appeared on McAfee’s show on Wednesday. He accused McCarthy of various things, such as sleeping through meetings, missing team activities, and breaking the team down by invoking the Green Bay Packers during halftime of a recent game. The fallout continues to reverberate through the NFL, with even Tom Brady weighing in on Thursday night. Pittsburgh, however, must keep its focus on the Broncos, who boast the sixth-best defense in the league, according to PFN’s Defense Impact Metric

item.title: Liga record setter Simeone's Atletico in pursuit of top two
item.description: Atletico Madrid coach Diego Simeone boasts more victories than any other manager in La Liga history (Javier SORIANO) No coach in the history of Spanish football has won more La Liga matches than Atletico Madrid's Diego Simeone. The Argentine claimed his 345th league victory last weekend to keep the Rojiblancos in the race to chase down Spain's traditional giants, Barcelona and Real Madrid. Third-placed Atletico visit Elche on Saturday with Simeone looking to keep adding to his record and deliver a third La Liga title, adding to his conquests in 2014 and 2021. Atletico trail leaders Barcelona by five points before they face the Catalans on December 2, in a match brought forward because of the teams' participation in the Spanish Super Cup in January. Barcelona visit Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday, while Real Madrid, second and two points ahead of Atletico, host Alaves on Saturday. Simeone surpassed the late Luis Aragones, on 344 league victories, to stand alone at the top of the all-time list. "I would like to share this number with all the people behind these 345 victories," said Simeone, speaking of his family, current and former staff and players. "I don't usually get excited about many things, but getting to this point has taken incredible work." Prying two league titles away from giants Real Madrid and Barcelona was an impressive achievement, and Atletico have shown this season they have the tools to do it again. Until their defeat by Barcelona before the international break, Atletico won their seven prior league matches, including a derby victory over Real Madrid. Their strong start has come without star player Julian Alvarez being at his best, which shows they can still find a higher gear. The Argentine forward wanted to leave in the summer and tried to force through a move to Barcelona, but Atletico staunchly resisted. Alvarez started the season at a low ebb and struggling for fitness, and has scored just three goals across all competitions to date. However the 2022 World Cup winner has started to show some of his quality in recent appearances and tensions with the supporters have eased. - 'Same ambition, hunger - Alvarez set up Atletico's first two goals against Getafe in their win last weekend and scored with a free-kick against Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday. "He's truly an incredible player, fantastic. I like him as a person, I'll support him as a footballer, I understand him as a player," said Simeone on Wednesday. "Even though he hasn't scored in previous matches, there isn't an attacking move that doesn't go through him, and he always contributes important things. To get where we want to be, we need the best Julian Alvarez." Simeone's other two title successes were powered by goals from South American strikers, with Brazilian Diego Costa key in 2014, and Uruguay's Luis Suarez vital in 2021. A resurgent Alvarez would help Atletico's bid for a third crown under Simeone. Atletico midfielder Koke said Simeone has not changed

"Obviously, he's a bit older but everything else remains the same... he's still very demanding in training, he doesn't let us relax for a second, and that's what makes the difference and allows us to compete against the best." rbs/gj

item.title: Bayern risk more than sporting success as Musiala saga rolls on
item.description: Jamal Musiala signals to the bench with injury. (Alexandra BEIER) Bayern Munich head to Hamburg on Saturday in the middle of a crisis which threatens not only to derail the club's sporting ambitions, but their identity itself. Bayern, who are in the midst of an injury crisis which has decimated their forward line including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, sit two points behind Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga table. But Bayern's treatment of midfielder Jamal Musiala by their hierarchy has led to a growing rift between the club and the playing group. Shortly after Bayern lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday, ending their run as the final unbeaten team in Europe's top-five leagues this season, vice-captain Joshua Kimmich suggested the club had fallen out of step with their values. "It's completely unacceptable and is not Bayern-like," Kimmich said on Wednesday, adding that Musiala's treatment was inconsistent with the club's "sense of togetherness". - 'Mia san mia' - This week, Bayern's hierarchy suggested Musiala take a pay cut as the 23-year-old battles his way back from a neurological condition which causes absence seizures. While the condemnation from media, player unions and former players was swift, Kimmich -- who was wearing the captain's armband with Manuel Neuer out injured -- was the first member of Bayern's current squad to speak out. Despite their status as one of football's perennial heavyweights, Bayern have always sought to emphasise their Bavarian roots and member-ownership in contrast to the American and Gulf-owned behemoths that loom over the European landscape. But their cold-hearted treatment of Musiala, a fan-favourite and popular inside the dressing room, threatens their carefully crafted identity. The club's vaunted 'Mia san mia' motto, which appears on every modern Bayern kit, translates to 'we are who we are'. Midfielder Aleksandar Pavlovic, a product of Bayern's youth system, in 2025 said: "For me, 'Mia san mia' means being a family, standing together in good times and bad. "That's what we live by here from a young age, that we always stick together." - Musiala's return - Just two months after signing a contract extension in February 2025, Musiala began treatment for symptoms of the neurological condition. After missing two months with an unrelated muscle injury, Musiala was warmly welcomed back by Bayern's 75,000-strong Allianz Arena on Friday. Minutes after full-time, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested Musiala's condition meant he might be unable to deliver on his lucrative deal and should take a pay cut. "If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation... because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable," he said. The firestorm began to spread immediately, with Bayern's untimely announcement of a record turnover of close to one billion euros ($1.1 billion) at their AGM a day later fanning the flames. On Saturday, international player union FIFPRO said that Bayern "should know better", identifying a void between the German giants' values and their behaviour. Former Bayern and Germany goalkeeper Oliver Kahn, who previously served as Bayern's CEO, issued a harsh critique. "To put the player under pressure now and appeal to his decency through the public sphere, urging him to forgo part of his salary, is simply absurd," Kahn said. But Kimmich's words have had the biggest impact as they provide a rare insight into the dressing room. "It is understandable that the club might be concerned because of the illness. What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated publicly," Kimmich said. "It must not happen that a player is made to bear the brunt of it." dwi/nf

item.title: Verstappen spells out what truly puts him off racing in the Indy 500
item.description: Max Verstappen has revealed why he is unwilling to take part in the Indianapolis 500, citing the risks associated with oval racing and the serious accident suffered by Nelson Piquet at Indianapolis. The four-time Formula 1 world champion has made no secret of his ambitions to compete in other motorsport disciplines alongside his commitments with Red Bull Racing, with endurance racing among the Dutchman's main interests. However, despite his admiration for the Indianapolis 500, Verstappen is not particularly interested in testing himself at the prestigious American event. The Red Bull driver explained that his reluctance has nothing to do with doubts over his ability to be competitive, but rather with the risks involved. Verstappen cites Piquet's Indianapolis crash Speaking to the media ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Verstappen pointed to the accident suffered by three-time F1 world champion Piquet, the father of his partner Kelly, as one of the reasons behind his stance. The Brazilian suffered serious injuries to both legs and feet during practice for the 1992 Indianapolis 500, requiring extensive surgery and months of rehabilitation. Despite the severity of his injuries, Piquet returned to Indianapolis the following year and qualified for the race. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen stressed that witnessing the long-term consequences of Piquet's accident has influenced his attitude towards competing in the American showpiece. "It's not that I think I won't be good at it. It's just the risk management. That's why I don't want to do it," Verstappen explained. "I like watching it, but I also know there is a very high risk involved by crashing, and I have had plenty of examples. "Even, of course, my father-in-law had a big crash there. And seeing how he had to live for the rest of his life after that crash is some risk that I'm not willing to take while already doing F1 and racing in GT3." The Dutchman also explained that, given the risks he already exposes himself to through his commitments in both Formula 1 and GT3 racing, he sees little reason to add another potentially dangerous undertaking to his schedule. "At one point, you're taking already a lot of risk. So sometimes then it's good to also have a few weekends where you don't need to be on the limit all the time."

item.title: Goo Goo Dolls Thanksgiving halftime show will not air on NBC during Bills vs. Chiefs game
item.description: NBC is making a surprising programming decision on Thanksgiving night. Instead of airing the highly anticipated live halftime performance of the Goo Goo Dolls, a Buffalo-based band, during the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs game, the network will air Mike Tirico’s sit-down interview with NBC analyst and former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin. While NFL fans may want to hear Tomlin’s take on the Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy saga, they do not want to hear it at halftime when live music is happening. As it stands, only fans in the stadium will see the show. MORE: Tom Brady takes dig at Aaron Rodgers amid Mike McCarthy drama Why is NBC doing this? Aug 25, 2026; Hollywood, FL, USA; Goo Goo Dolls Summer 2026 Tour with John Rzeznik (Guitar and Vocals) and Robby Takac (Bass) at Hard Rock Live, Hollywood, Florida on August 25, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Ron Elkman-Imagn Images Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) NBC is banking on the fact that television viewers want to hear about Aaron Rodgers more than the Goo Goo Dolls. I will be very sad if we don’t get to see the Goo Goo Dolls perform in the rain 🙏 — Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) November 27, 2026 Every NFL media analyst who worked today, including Tom Brady, Rob Gronkowski, Terry Bradshaw, and Russell Wilson, condemned Rogers for his tell-all interview on ESPN’s “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday. Tomlin’s take could be predictably similar with the only added benefit of knowing the inner workings of the Steelers organization better than the rest. MORE: Art Rooney II backs Steelers’ Mike McCarthy, rips Aaron Rodgers in scathing statement Goo Goo Dolls’ NFL performance For those who want to hear the Goo Goo Dolls in an NFL setting, turn back time with the video from a 2003 Super Bowl event. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

Tomlin’s take could be predictably similar with the only added benefit of knowing the inner workings of the Steelers organization better than the rest. item.title: UConn Men's Basketball: Dan Hurley Addresses Future of Huskies-Duke Rivalry
item.description:
The UConn Huskies men's basketball team suffered its second consecutive loss on Wednesday night, dropping a neutral site contest against the Duke Blue Devils. With the loss, the Huskies are now 4-2 on the season, having also lost to Arizona last Wednesday. While UConn still remains as one of the best teams in the country, especially with Solo Ball returning to the lineup, it is clearly trying to figure out how to play without Nik Khamenia, who is out with injury. The UConn-Duke showdown, played in Las Vegas, was one of the most highly-anticipated games of the college hoops season, but UConn head coach Dan Hurley seems to want it played in a different setting moving forward. The announced crowd of 8,500 was clearly good, but Hurley said afterwards that maybe the game would do better if it were a home-and-home series involving trips to Durham, N.C. and Storrs, Conn. He even mentioned the idea of playing the game at Madison Square Garden, suggesting that that venue would be better equipped to sell the game out. What would a home-and-home series mean for the rivalry? Simply put? It would be electric for the fans of both programs. The most fun college games are played on individual campuses or at campus-adjacent team arenas, but who knows if that can actually happen. Often times, neutral site games are worth more money to television networks, so maybe a game at Madison Square Garden is more logical. UConn is playing a ridiculously hard non-conference schedule this season, but only the game against Kansas on Dec. 12 is being played on camps at Gampel Pavilion. UConn Huskies head coach Dan Hurley talks to the referee during the first half against the Arizona Wildcats at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena. Aryanna Frank-Imagn Images
What's next for this UConn team? The Huskies are back in action on Monday night against Rider as they ease back into the non-conference schedule after the Thanksgiving holiday. And how about the rest of UConn Athletics? 1) Well, the UConn football team will close out the regular season on Saturday afternoon (noon ET) against Wyoming. The Huskies are 6-5 while the Cowboys are 7-4. UConn is already bowl-eligible, but it isn't guaranteed a bowl game berth at this time. Winning a seventh game on the season would go a long way toward guaranteeing that. 2) The UConn women's basketball team will take on No. 5 Duke on Saturday night at 7 p.m. ET. The Blue Devils are coached by Kara Lawson, who helped lead Team USA to a FIBA World Cup gold medal this summer.

item.title: Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin to address Aaron Rodgers' exit: Live updates
item.description: It may be Thanksgiving. It may be a day removed from Aaron Rodgers' stunning divorce from the Pittsburgh Steelers , who will host the Denver Broncos for the league's now-annual Black Friday game. But the four-time NFL MVP and, suddenly, NFL free agent remains at the forefront of the discourse around the league and even the country in the aftermath of his very public exposure of Steelers coach Mike McCarthy's alleged issues and why they drove Rodgers to the point of issuing ultimatums and later detailing just about everything going in the Pittsburgh locker room in a remarkable break from NFL protocol − and Rodgers' long-held belief that matters that swirl about a football team's inner sanctum should remain private. But after 24 hours of pundits, reporters, social media, Rodgers' former teammates and a handful of current ones weighing in, a man with a perspective as unique and, for the most part, as informed as any is about to share his thoughts regarding the shocking meltdown that's occurred in the Steel City. Mike Tomlin, the Steelers' coach for 19 seasons and perhaps the primary reason Rodgers came to Pittsburgh a year ago, is set to discuss what's happened to the Steelers at halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs- Buffalo Bills game in his current as an analyst for NBC. This story will be updated with his thoughts. JARRETT BELL: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers strip each other of graceful endings. Go figure | Opinion What did Aaron Rodgers say about Mike Tomlin? While questioning McCarthy's dedication and efficacy at his job Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show," Rodgers took the opportunity to praise Tomlin anew. Both he and his former coach had long had mutual admiration before teaming up for the 2025 season. But Tomlin stepped down at the end of the campaign, which ended with a resounding loss in the wild-card round to the Houston Texans in Pittsburgh. Per reports, Rodgers was in tears when Tomlin announced the decision to leave his post in the aftermath of the loss. "Leader of men, he knew everybody’s name, knew where they came from," Rodgers said of Tomlin on Wednesday, a comment that also served to distinguish him from McCarthy. "Different mentality." All the NFL news on and off the field. Sign up for USA TODAY's 4th and Monday newsletter . This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin to address Aaron Rodgers' exit: Live updates

item.title: Ravens’ Derrick Henry injury upgrade is great news for Texans game
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Ravens’ Derrick Henry injury upgrade is great news for Texans game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens finally caught a break heading into their road clash with the Houston Texans, as Derrick Henry appears to be trending toward playing on Sunday. Henry, who is in the concussion protocol, was a full participant in Thursday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday , according to the team’s official injury report . It’s a promising sign for the veteran running back. The 32-year-old landed hard in the end zone after scoring a 15-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter of Baltimore’s 35-33 loss to the Carolina Panthers last Sunday. He initially passed his checks but was later placed in the protocol. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Even so, head coach Jesse Minter sounded confident earlier this week that Henry would be available. “He had a couple of brief symptoms of a concussion right towards the end of that game,” Minter said, via Jamison Hensley. “We do expect him to be back obviously.” Henry will still need to clear the final steps of the protocol before he is officially good to go. Baltimore will need all the help it can get. The Ravens have dropped six straight games , which tied the second-longest losing streak in franchise history, and sit at 4-7 on the season. They have also been without Lamar Jackson, who is sidelined with a thumb injury, forcing Jacoby Brissett into the starting role . Henry has been one of the few bright spots for Baltimore this season. The two-time rushing champion has piled up 793 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns through 11 games. He was productive against the Panthers, too, rushing for 94 yards and a score on 13 carries while adding four catches for 17 yards. The Ravens also got positive news on Zay Flowers, who was upgraded from limited to full on Thursday as he deals with an ankle issue. Defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike, however, missed practice again with a hamstring injury. Houston, meanwhile, enters the matchup at 4-6 and fresh off a 26-3 rout of the Indianapolis Colts . item.title: Tom Brady sounds off on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy drama: ‘Nobody wins’
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Tom Brady sounds off on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy drama: ‘Nobody wins’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Aaron Rodgers shook up Thanksgiving week with his scorched earth rant about Mike McCarthy and the Pittsburgh Steelers . Legends like Terry Bradshaw lit into Rodgers Thursday . But even his fellow Fox colleague Tom Brady chimed in. Brady shared a “nobody wins” take once asked about his thoughts on the Rodgers/Steelers fallout. “I just think in response to that, the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place. We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players,” Brady began. “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room because you’re fighting with your teammates and your coaches. You’re fighting as a team together. But it shouldn’t be the place for private things to become public.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brady then weighed in on the legacy of Rodgers now that he’s been released. “I mean, hall of fame career and he’s a tremendous player. It has nothing to do with his play style. I was fortunate to play with some great teammates over the years. What made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and coaches and you cared about what your team is about to accomplish. And that super cedes any individual aspect that you want to promote. I played for my teammates, my coaches, but nobody wins when the family feuds.” Tom Brady just addressed the Aaron Rodgers/ Mike McCarthy mess in Pittsburgh on the FOX broadcast. “Nobody wins when the family feuds.” His full comments: pic.twitter.com/CChvIe0FrF — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 Rodgers even played in an era where Brady guided six Super Bowl wins with the New England Patriots, then added one more with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Brady’s Bucs team even denied Rodgers’ Packers an NFC title during the 2020 season. Rodgers ripped McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show, accusing the coach of “snoring” during team meetings. Then vowed he wouldn’t play for the Steelers after saying Pittsburgh wouldn’t allow him to call the plays. item.title: Australia squad for New Zealand Test series 2026: Full team lists for AUS vs NZ red-ball series as Nathan Lyon is set to be dropped
item.description: Australia squad for New Zealand Test series 2026: Full team lists for AUS vs NZ red-ball series as Nathan Lyon is set to be dropped originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australia will soon reveal their squad for the Perth Test against New Zealand. Nathan Lyon is reportedly set to miss out. Recent Sheffield Shield numbers have added fresh pressure on the long-serving veteran's place. End of an era in Australian cricket! 577-wicket legend Nathan Lyon set to be axed from Test squad for New Zealand series Australia's squad for the New Zealand Test series is about to be named, and the biggest talking point is the likely absence of Nathan Lyon. According to a report from Tom Decent of The Sydney Morning Herald , the veteran off-spinner won't find his name on the list for the series opener in Perth. Lyon is 39 now, and his place in the side hasn't been a certainty over the last few series. He was left out of the second Test in South Africa, with Scott Boland picked in his place, which was an early hint that things were shifting. Last summer's Ashes Test in Perth offers a useful clue about how the team management views him at home. Lyon sent down only two overs in that match, because Australia's fast bowlers bowled England out twice inside two days. He then missed the day-night Test at the Gabba that followed. He came back for Adelaide, but a hamstring injury ended his series there, which interrupted a run that had looked untouchable for years. The South Africa tour further added to his misery. In the final Test in Cape Town, his counterpart Simon Harmer won the game for the hosts with 6 for 16 in the second innings and 10 for 120 across the match. Lyon picked up four wickets in the same game, but the contrast with Harmer was hard to miss. After that Cape Town defeat, head coach Andrew McDonald was asked whether Lyon's standing as first-choice spinner would be looked at again. "I don't think it's something to review now," McDonald said. "I think we sit back and we'll go through Shield cricket. Nathan will be preparing for the first Test match in Perth." MORE: Khawaja admits speaking earlier would have ended career; Smith told him to 'shut up' Predicted Australia Squad for New Zealand Test series 2026 Pat Cummins (c) Travis Head Matt Renshaw Steve Smith Jack Clayton Sam Konstas Cameron Green Josh Inglis Cooper Connolly Alex Carey (wk) Mitchell Starc Josh Hazlewood Scott Boland Mitchell Swepson Matt Kuhnemann Sheffield Shield form: Mitchell Swepson and Corey Rocchiccioli in the spotlight Domestic form hasn't helped Lyon's case. In the latest Sheffield Shield game at the SCG, he took four wickets, but Queensland legspinner Mitchell Swepson claimed 11 and looked far more threatening on a turning surface. Swepson now leads the wicket-takers' chart this season. Western Australia's Corey Rocchiccioli is fifth, and he also hit his maiden first-class century in his most recent outing. Lyon

Lyon sent down only two overs in that match, because Australia's fast bowlers bowled England out twice inside two days. He then missed the day-night Test at the Gabba that followed. In the final Test in Cape Town, his counterpart Simon Harmer won the game for the hosts with 6 for 16 in the second innings and 10 for 120 across the match. Lyon picked up four wickets in the same game, but the contrast with Harmer was hard to miss. After that Cape Town defeat, head coach Andrew McDonald was asked whether Lyon's standing as first-choice spinner would be looked at again. "I don't think it's something to review now," McDonald said. "I think we sit back and we'll go through Shield cricket. Nathan will be preparing for the first Test match in Perth." MORE: Khawaja admits speaking earlier would have ended career; Smith told him to 'shut up' Predicted Australia Squad for New Zealand Test series 2026 Pat Cummins (c) Travis Head Matt Renshaw Steve Smith Jack Clayton Sam Konstas Cameron Green Josh Inglis Cooper Connolly Alex Carey (wk) Mitchell Starc Josh Hazlewood Scott Boland Mitchell Swepson Matt Kuhnemann Sheffield Shield form: Mitchell Swepson and Corey Rocchiccioli in the spotlight Domestic form hasn't helped Lyon's case. In the latest Sheffield Shield game at the SCG, he took four wickets, but Queensland legspinner Mitchell Swepson claimed 11 and looked far more threatening on a turning surface. Swepson now leads the wicket-takers' chart this season. Western Australia's Corey Rocchiccioli is fifth, and he also hit his maiden first-class century in his most recent outing. Lyon has collected 577 Test wickets for Australia since his debut in 2011, which leaves only Shane Warne ahead of him on the country's all-time list. Any decision to leave him out would therefore mark the end of a long era. Australia must back form over reputation in the Lyon decision Dropping a bowler with 577 Test wickets is never easy, and the emotion around Nathan Lyon is understandable. Still, selection has to be about the present, not the past, and the present picture is mixed. He has been dropped twice in recent months; he bowled just two overs in the Perth Ashes Test, and he was outshone by Simon Harmer in Cape Town. The Shield numbers tell the same story. Mitchell Swepson took 11 wickets in the match where Lyon took four, and he sits on top of the season's list with 24. Corey Rocchiccioli has also shown he can contribute, with wickets and a maiden hundred. That said, Australia shouldn't be too hasty. Lyon's experience and control have won countless Tests, and McDonald's own words suggested the door wasn't closed. If the Perth pitch suits pace, leaving him out may be a tactical call and not a verdict on his career. The real test comes when the surface turns, in Adelaide or Sydney, because Australia will need a trusted spinner then. If Swepson or Rocchiccioli gets the nod and thrives, the selectors will have found a successor in good time. If they struggle, Lyon's record will look even stronger in hindsight. Either way, change was always going to come, and handling it well matters more than the timing. Head to the comments section to give us your views on this story and share your opinion with our Cricket News Community, or you can visit our Facebook , Instagram , and X (Twitter) pages.

item.title: National reaction from Cowboys-Eagles: Brian Schottenheimer ‘out of his depth’ as NFL coach
item.description: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer walks the field after losing an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington. (Elías Valverde II/The Dallas Morning News) Is this the final nail in the coffin for Brian Schottenheimer? His Dallas Cowboys completed their trifecta of miserable home-field collapses on Thursday , coughing up a 21-point lead to the two-win Eagles and falling 39-38 on a last-second field goal . The loss had everything the Cowboys have become known for under Brian Schottenheimer: Terrible defense, baffling play calls, an overwhelming number of penalties and, finally, a failure to win even two games in a row. This might be the one that does Cowboys fans in. The calls for Schottenheimer's job, already loud, are becoming deafening. Check out the best reactions from the loss on a not-so-happy Thanksgiving below. #DallasCowboys https://t.co/aJE6o0Joxc — [Official] P1Domo (@P1Domo) November 27, 2026 What exactly were the cowboys doing there — Caitlin Clark (@CaitlinClark22) November 27, 2026 The largest Thanksgiving comeback in #NFL history. https://t.co/3QMhXj1UH7 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 27, 2026 🚨 EAGLES BEAT COWBOYS ON A GAME-WINNING FIELD GOAL DALLAS BLOWS A 21-POINT LEAD ON THANKSGIVING (Via @NFL) https://t.co/KHc9ALVb7m — Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) November 27, 2026 The Eagles secure the largest Thanksgiving comeback win in NFL history! 🦅 According to ESPN Analytics the Cowboys had a 99.4% win probability after the Brandon Aubrey FG at 3:35 in the 3rd quarter! 😱 https://t.co/O63jny2VTA — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 27, 2026 Inexcusable. The Cowboys lose 39-38. They are now 0-5 this season when they had the chance to win a second-consecutive game. The defining trait of the Brian Schottenheimer Era continues to be inconsistency. — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) November 27, 2026 That’s a job killer, or at the least a mortal wound. — Brad Townsend (@townbrad) November 27, 2026 That should be the last straw — Evan Grant (@Evan_P_Grant) November 27, 2026 Maybe Jerry should wake up Mike McCarthy and ask him if he wants to come back? — Mike Doocy (@MikeDoocyFox4) November 27, 2026 Shotgun and this playcall on 4th-and-1 is a disgrace. https://t.co/oaROUDeEpi — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 What a failure the Brian Schottenheimer hire was and has been. Setting new records for embarrassment each week at this point. — CJ Vogel (@CJVogel_OTF) November 27, 2026 Nah I promise I’m not watching next season if Brian Schottenheimer is still the head coach. This team has lost to: 3-7 Buccaneers 3-8 Cardinals 4-7 Eagles All at home. — nicky (@PFF_Nicky) November 27, 2026 Brian Schottenheimer shouldn’t be a head coach in the NFL. He’s out of his depth. I don’t know what else needs to be seen. Some guys just aren’t cut out to be head coaches and he’s one of them. He brings nothing to the table. — Nick Coppola (@Nick_Coppola__) November 27,

item.title: Christian Mahogany Suggests NFL Investigate Chicago Bears Following Thanksgiving Game
item.description: The Detroit Lions’ heartbreaking 39-35 Thanksgiving Day loss to the Chicago Bears may have featured more controversy than initially realized. Following Thursday’s game at Ford Field, Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany accused the Bears’ defense of simulating Detroit’s snap count, contributing to costly false-start penalties. While Mahogany acknowledged that the Lions ultimately have to take responsibility for their mistakes, he also suggested that the NFL has the means to investigate what was being said on the field. Detroit Lions offensive line coach Hank Fraley talk to offensive lineman Christian Mahogany (73) after a play against Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Christian Mahogany Accuses Chicago Bears of Simulating Snap Count During the first half of Thursday’s game, the Lions were flagged for back-to-back false-start penalties on two separate occasions. Following the game, Mahogany explained that he believed Chicago’s defenders were intentionally mimicking quarterback Jared Goff’s cadence to get Detroit’s offensive linemen to move prematurely. “They’re simulating the snap count,” Mahogany told the Detroit Free Press . “They’re using − they find out the snap count of the quarterback and they use it, and that’s it. They use the words. So like I said, no bitching and complaining, we self-inflicted those wounds and we can’t false start.” According to the official NFL rulebook , defensive players are prohibited from using words or actions intended to disrupt the offense’s signals at the snap. Such conduct falls under the league’s unsportsmanlike conduct rules. Mahogany Says NFL Has Ability to Investigate Perhaps the most interesting part of Mahogany’s comments came when he revealed that multiple Detroit offensive linemen were wearing microphones during the game. According to Mahogany, those recordings could provide the NFL with evidence of what was being said along the line of scrimmage. “We wear mics,” Mahogany said. “I wear a mic, Tate [Ratledge] wears a mic. They’re going to be able to hear and they can investigate themselves on what was said.” Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, however, denied the allegations following the game . Whether the NFL elects to review the recordings remains to be seen, and there has been no confirmed announcement of a league investigation. Detroit Lions Cannot Afford Costly Mistakes Heading into Thursday’s game, Dan Campbell emphasized the significance of the Thanksgiving showdown . Unfortunately, the Lions squandered an 11-point fourth-quarter lead, snapping their six-game winning streak and surrendering sole possession of first place in the NFC North to Chicago. Detroit also missed an opportunity to reverse a remarkable historical trend dating back to 1934 . Instead, the Lions are left wondering how a game that appeared to be firmly in their control slipped away. To Mahogany’s credit,

item.title: ‘Your Past Self Would Be Embarrassed To See What You’ve Amounted To’ — Emmanuel Acho Rips Former ESPN Star Over Criticism of Aaron Rodgers Comments
item.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers shook the football world out of slumber on Wednesday. His appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show” sent the Pittsburgh Steelers into disarray and ultimately led to his release from the team. It has also had a huge ripple effect across the game. Rodgers vented some frustrations with head coach Mike McCarthy, making several accusations about his former sideline boss. Some of them were confirmed by insiders and even McCarthy himself. This situation has everyone talking and has even ignited social media beef between two media personalities within the NFL world. NFL Analysts Clash Amid Fallout From Aaron Rodgers Interview As this situation evolved, former linebacker Emmanuel Acho spoke to some people within the game to get their reactions. One conversation he had was with former Green Bay Packers receiver James Jones. It was this segment that upset former ESPN analyst Trey Wingo, who took to social media to share criticisms of Acho. “Just your reminder that Acho was the same dude that said Shedeur Sanders… the current backup in Cleveland for the 6-4 Browns… shouldn’t listen to anything his head coach says. Translated? If Acho turns left, you should probably turn right,” Wingo said on social media . Suffice it to say, Acho wasn’t pleased with these comments. The former Philadelphia Eagles LB hit back at Wingo on social media, making some scathing comments regarding the state of his career. “Just a reminder, your best days are behind you. Nobody watches your content anymore. You’re an old, bitter, senile has-been who hasn’t recovered from ESPN moving on from him. Your once illustrious career has dissolved into that of a glorified Twitter troll, yet you get no glory from trolling. Your past self would be embarrassed to see what you’ve amounted to. I am. Seek help. Happy Thanksgiving,” Acho wrote . PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Wingo was a former analyst at ESPN. He joined the network in 1997, lending his voice and analysis to multiple projects across his lengthy career there. He left ESPN in 2020. The Rodgers situation began on Tuesday night. The Steelers made an announcement at 11:10 that night that they were going to bench Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph in Week 12. This led to his appearance on McAfee’s show. Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep during meetings, missing team activities, and mistakenly using a Packers chant at halftime against Philadelphia. Unnamed sources corroborated portions of Rodgers’ account, while McCarthy publicly acknowledged the halftime incident. Rodgers also stated multiple times that he had no interest in playing for Pittsburgh again after how things ended. Pittsburgh proceeded to release him on Wednesday following his comments. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer It has certainly been a chaotic week for the Steelers organization.
