item.title: “He Wasn’t a Perfect Coach”: Tom Brady Makes Honest Admission on Bill Belichick After Calling Out Aaron Rodgers During FOX NFL Broadcast
item.description: Tom Brady ©IMAGO/Pacific Press Agency The entire NFL community is talking about Aaron Rodgers and his unexpected exit from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Even during the live broadcast of the Week 12 game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles on FOX Sports, Tom Brady and Kevin Burkhardt couldn’t steer away from talking about Rodgers’ ugly breakup. The beef between Rodgers and Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy later urged Brady to talk about his own troubles with the coaching staff. During his time with the New England Patriots , Brady had a few disputes with Bill Belichick. But at the end of the day, they won six Super Bowls together. “I wasn’t a perfect player. He wasn’t a perfect coach,” Brady weighed in on his relationship with Belichick . “But we did some things in the game that we’re so proud of now. “Even me being four years removed from the game, the things that matter more than winning a Super Bowl trophy [are] my relationships with my teammates, my coaches. That’s gonna transcend anything you do. So it’s just unfortunate. I hate it. I hate to be even talking about it. I just think, you know, it’s a privilege in the NFL. You want to inspire the next generation of athletes. You always want to do it the right way.” Brady's candid take on Belichick and Rodgers reveals the real dynamics behind NFL greatness. Subscribe to stay ahead of the biggest quarterback narratives and insider perspectives. During his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, Rodgers reacted to being benched ahead of Friday’s Week 12 game against the Denver Broncos. He was clearly upset about letting Mason Rudolph replace him and questioned the Steelers’ head coach. Ultimately, the comments forced the Steelers to release the 42-year-old. Needless to say, Brady wasn’t pleased with the unrest between Rodgers and McCarthy. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place. And we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. It shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say.” Brady further added that Rodgers certainly has a Hall of Fame career but did not condone the public nature of the disputes that led to his split from the Steelers. He claimed that the dispute against McCarthy and the Steelers had nothing to do with the 42-year-old quarterback’s playing style. Meanwhile, the seven-time Super Bowl champion claimed that he was “fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years.” According to him, caring about one’s teammates and coaches makes a player a great teammate. And that takes higher priority over any individual aspect of the game that the players wish to promote. “I was very fortunate,” Brady went on. “I was in a great locker room; I played for my teammates; I played for my coaches. … Nobody wins when the family feuds.” Brady’s candid reflectio

item.title: California’s Top High School Basketball Forwards, Centers to Watch in 2026-27
item.description: Tarek Fattal California’s high school basketball frontcourt is loaded with size and talent entering the 2026-27 season. The group features nationally ranked prospects, college commits, emerging big men and a pair of seven-footers at St. Francis who could make the Golden Knights one of the state’s toughest teams to handle inside. Class Of 2027 Emmanuel Ahamefule, Archbishop Riordan (PF) — The 6-foot-9 power forward is a nationally ranked prospect in the 2027 class, checking in at No. 129 overall in the Rivals Industry rankings. Ahamefule gives Archbishop Riordan a sizable frontcourt presence, although publicly available statistics from last season are limited. Mahamadou Diop, San Gabriel Academy (C) — Diop is a 6-foot-11 center who has already made his college decision, committing to San Diego State. He earned first-team All-Area honors from the San Gabriel Valley Tribune after his junior season and is ranked among California’s top frontcourt prospects. Cherif Millogo, St. Francis (C) — At 7-foot-5, Millogo is one of the most imposing prospects in the country. He averaged 24.8 points, 11.4 rebounds, 5.1 blocks and 3.8 assists last season, earned second-team MaxPreps Junior All-America honors and signed with Kentucky in November. King Rachal, Notre Dame (SF) — Rachal is a 6-foot-7 wing who signed with Utah State after drawing interest from multiple high-major programs. The Rivals Industry ranks him No. 45 nationally, and he joins a Notre Dame team that also features fellow 2027 standout NaVorro Bowman Jr. Nick Welch, Rolling Hills Prep (PF) — Welch is a 6-foot-9 forward ranked No. 132 nationally in the Rivals Industry rankings. He was identified by the Los Angeles Times as a player ready to take a significant step forward this season. Class Of 2028 Owen Eteuati-Edwards, Arcadia (PF) — The 6-foot-8 forward is coming off a productive sophomore season in which he averaged 14.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game. Eteuati-Edwards is a versatile frontcourt player who can contribute as a scorer, rebounder and facilitator. Yann Kamagate, St. Francis (C) — Kamagate has quickly become one of the most highly regarded players in the country, ranking No. 1 nationally in the 2028 Rivals Industry rankings. The 7-footer averaged 14.3 points and 9.3 rebounds at the NBPA Top 100 Camp, then opened the high school season with a 29-point, 20-rebound performance against Palisades. Jakobi Oware, St. Pius X-St. Matthias Academy (SF) — Oware is a 6-foot-6 wing ranked No. 26 nationally in the 2028 Rivals Industry rankings. He also earned an invitation to the October 2026 USA Basketball Men’s Junior National Team minicamp, another indication of his standing among the country’s rising prospects. Houston Rolle, Sierra Canyon (SF) — Rolle is a 6-foot wing ranked No. 52 nationally in the Rivals Industry rankings. He joins a Sierra Canyon program that annually competes for Southern Section and state championships, giving him a prominent platform to continue developing.

item.title: ESPN's Laura Rutledge Melts Hearts With Heartwarming Thanksgiving Message
item.description: FOXBOROUGH, MA – DECEMBER 01: ESPN Monday Night FootballÕs sideline reporter Laura Rutledge before a game between the New England Patriots and the New York Giants on December 1, 2025, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA DEC 01 Giants at Patriots EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon482251201109 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Laura Rutledge spends most of the year covering the biggest moments in college football and the NFL, often away from home while families gather to watch. But Thanksgiving gave the ESPN host a chance to share a more personal side of her life. Rutledge posted family pictures on X with her husband, their two children and their dogs, along with a heartfelt holiday message. “Happy Thanksgiving from our family to yours! Sending all of you so much love. So grateful,” Rutledge’s X post caption read. The pictures showed the Rutledges posing together on the staircase at their home in Connecticut. Her husband, Josh Rutledge, is a former MLB infielder who played for the Rockies and the Red Sox. They met in 2011 at a football weekend in Tuscaloosa and married in December 2013. Josh is now a real estate agent in the Hartford area. Their daughter, Reese, 7, was born on October 2, 2019, the same day as Laura’s birthday, and their son, Jack, was born in May 2023. Followers of Laura’s social feeds know the kids as the college football pickers, as Reese and Jack have made Saturday picks on her account for years. Laura Rutledge's genuine gratitude resonates beyond the broadcast booth. Subscribe to stay connected with the human moments that make college football unforgettable. The Thanksgiving post comes after a heavy few weeks. item.title: Dorival Júnior announces he will leave São Paulo in 2027
item.description: Dorival Júnior announces he will leave São Paulo in 2027 Coach Dorival Júnior announced on Thursday (26) that he will not be in charge of São Paulo in 2027. He made the announcement during a press conference after the 3–1 win over Remo in the Brasileirão. His farewell will come in the final round of the championship, away to Athletico-PR, next Wednesday (2). Shortly afterward, club executive Rafinha also announced that he would be leaving the Tricolor. Sorry for the delay. We were informing the players, the president and the staff that we will be staying until the final match of this year's Brazilian league. After that, it is important that we leave the club so that the future presidential candidates can choose their own staff Dorival Júnior São Paulo's presidential election is scheduled for December and, according to ge, other decisions at the club depend on who wins the vote. Dorival Júnior's tenure Dorival returned to the Tricolor in May on a contract running only until the end of this year. He took over after Roger Machado was sacked at the start of the Brasileirão. This is Dorival's third spell at the Morumbi club. His first was between 2017 and 2018, while his second was his most successful, winning the Copa do Brasil in 2023. Rafinha's tenure Rafinha's time at São Paulo was even shorter. The former player was announced as football executive in July, shortly before the end of the Brasileirão's World Cup break. The position had been vacant since Rui Costa's departure in June. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Bears stun Lions, Eagles rally in NFL Thanksgiving thrillers
item.description: Chicago's Rome Odunze celebrates his game-winning touchdown catch with Bears teammate Kalif Raymond after the team's NFL win over the Detroit Lions (Gregory Shamus) Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a game-winning touchdown with three seconds remaining on Thursday as the Chicago Bears beat the Detroit Lions 39-35 in an NFL Thanksgiving holiday thriller. Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze -- who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone -- gave the Bears their first lead of the game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions. "We knew we needed a big one," Odunze said. "Luckily the O-line held up for me. Caleb delivered the ball exactly where it needed to be, and I was able to make a play in the back of the end zone." Williams connected on 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns -- both to Odunze. The Bears had two rushing touchdowns from Kyle Monangai and one from D'Andre Swift to help offset a monster game from Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who ran for 205 yards and three TDs. The Bears erased an early 10-point deficit, knotting it at 10-10 on Monangai's first touchdown with 4:07 left in the first half. Jared Goff hit Sam LaPorta with an 11-yard scoring pass to push Detroit's lead to 19-10 going into halftime, but Monangai's two-yard TD had the Bears back within two, minutes into the third quarter. The Lions finally appeared to be in control after Gibbs motored 70 yards for a touchdown that gave Detroit a 35-24 lead with 8:20 remaining. Chicago responded with a three-play, 71-yard drive capped by Williams's 41-yard scoring pass to Odunze. Detroit's next possession ended with a Goff interception, the Lions coming up empty on two straight possessions before the Bears put together their game-winning drive. - Elliott lifts Eagles - In Dallas, the Philadelphia Eagles erased a 21-point third-quarter deficit to beat the Cowboys 39-38. Jake Elliott drilled a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining for Philadelphia, who scored 22 points in the fourth quarter. "A lot of adversity, a lot of things we had to battle through," Elliott said. "This team just keeps showing up. Every single week we keep fighting." The Eagles' game-winning drive came after the Cowboys, leading by two, opted to go for it on fourth-and-one with 55 seconds left. Quarterback Dak Prescott was sacked and the Eagles capitalized. Philadelphia quarterback Joe Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to DeVonta Smith, and ran for another TD. Prescott threw for 291 yards and two touchdowns, but special teams miscues hurt the Cowboys. The Eagles scored a touchdown off a blocked punt and Dallas kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the final period. The three-game holiday slate concluded with a heavyweight AFC showdown between Patrick Mahomes's Kansas City Chiefs and Josh Allen's Bills in Buffalo. bb/pnb

item.title: Here is where the Cowboys fit in the NFC East division race after Thanksgiving
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are a broken football team. They had a win firmly in their hands and just handed back to the Philadelphia Eagles. Brian Schottenheimer fell apart in the fourth quarter with several awful decisions. Once again they played for a field goal late in the game instead of being aggressive and playing for the touchdown to win the game. Then they made a baffling call on fourth down – instead of kicking a field goal, or running the ball for one yard, they called a pass. Disaster when Dak Prescott was sacked leading to a long field goal from the Eagles to win 39-38. The Cowboys are now done for the year and are just going to play out the string. It was an embarrassing loss, one they need to accept as an impetus for change. They can’t continue running this back in the same form any longer. item.title: How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident
item.description: By Esther Onyegbulam, Matthew Johnson & Patrick Chidubem Six persons were burnt to death, while 12 others sustained varying degrees of burns yesterday after a commercial vehicle caught fire at Magbon, along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, which confirmed the incident, said the victims comprised two females and four males, all adults. It added that the 12 injured persons were rescued and taken to Badagry General Hospital for medical attention. However, an eyewitness account shared in a video gave a different initial account of the tragedy, claiming that many people were feared dead, with only two occupants, reportedly the driver and another passenger, surviving the incident. According to the eyewitness, the accident occurred between 8am and 9am and involved a commercial bus travelling from Mile 2 towards Badagry. The incident reportedly happened shortly after Checking Point Bus Stop, before the Black Signboard axis of the expressway. The eyewitness account indicated that the vehicle caught fire, resulting in multiple casualties. However, the initial casualty figures could not be independently verified. In its official account, the Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, said the agency received a distress call at 8:44am, while firefighters from its Badagry station arrived at the scene at 9:13am. According to Adeseye, “Preliminary information gathered during the investigation indicated that the driver reportedly had an additional five litres of fuel stored inside the vehicle, intending to refuel the vehicle’s tank. The presence of the extra fuel is suspected to have contributed to the intensity of the fire. “Tragically, six persons, comprising two females and four males, all adults, were involved in the incident. All six victims were burnt beyond recognition,” the statement said. Vanguard News The post How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, Justice for survivors
item.description: *Mrs Sanwo-Olu hails centre’s 10,000-Survivor Care Milestone By Henry Ojelu THE United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have called for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said the achievement deserved celebration but stressed that sexual violence remained a serious issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” Baxter emphasised the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, saying their voices were essential to understanding their challenges and improving access to support and justice. He reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to ending violence against women and girls through development partnerships and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. He also disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches and solutions. Earlier, Eze-Anaba acknowledged the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission to the establishment and growth of the centre. She said the British High Commission funded the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and advocacy opportunities. Describing the milestone as more than a numerical achievement, she said the centre remained committed to delivering services with dignity and respect. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors and had engaged an independent consultant to assess its services, identify gaps and recommend improvements. She thanked the centre’s partners and funders, assuring that it would continue to provide compassionate care where survivors’ voices mattered. Sanwo-Olu Hails Centre’s Milestone Meanwhile, Lagos State First Lady, Mrs Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, has commended the Mirabel Centre for supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence, describing the achievement as a significant contribution to the fight against gender-based violence. Sanwo-Olu, who launched the publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters, announced the donation of five copies each to all primary healthcare centres in Lagos State. She said support for survivors should extend beyond medical treatment and court proceedings to include counselling, continuous care and interventions to help them rebuild their lives. According to her, survivors need sustained support to heal and live better lives, while prevention should receive as much attention as treatment and rehabilitation. The First Lady said she had championed advocacy against gender-based violence through partnerships with government and non-governmental organisations, including the establishment of an inter-ministerial stakeholders’ committee in 2020. She also called for greater efforts to educate children from an early age to reject violence and respect others. item.title: 18.3m children out of school: Stakeholders demand urgent action
item.description: … NGE challenges govt, media, private sector as UNICEF warns on first 1,000 days By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners yesterday called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million children out of school in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. item.content:encoded: … NGE challenges govt, media, private sector as UNICEF warns on first 1,000 days By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners yesterday called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million children out of school in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF Representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. She urged journalists to go beyond reporting statistics and highlight the experiences of vulnerable children and families. “Statistics only matter when they move us to protect the child behind the number. We need the media to humanize the numbers, keep children in the headlines year-round and spotlight the solutions that are working across Nigeria,” she said. In her keynote address, Lagos State First Lady, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, said supporting mothers and investing early in children were essential to building a healthier and better-educated generation. She said the Babajide Sanwo-Olu administration remained committed to inclusive child development and gender-responsive governance, ensuring that every child, irrespective of gender, had the opportunity to realise his or her potential. On the proposed review of the Lagos State Child’s Rights Law 2015, she said: “As we undertake the review of the Child’s Rights Law 2015, we have before us a unique opportunity to strengthen our legal and institutional framework in ways that respond to emerging realities while safeguarding the best interests of every child.” Providing further insight into the child health situation, Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Primary Health Care Board, Dr Ibrahim Akinwunmi-Mustafa, said Nigeria had made progress in reducing under-five mortality but continued to face serious challenges in newborn survival and childhood malnutrition. “Under-five deaths have fallen from 132 to 110 per 1,000 live births since 2018. But newborn deaths have barely moved, and four in ten Nigerian children are still stunted.” He disclosed that child stunting in Lagos was about 17 per cent, compared with 40 per cent nationally, while an estimated 120,000 to 130,000 children in the state had never received a single vaccine. “Most of them live in our informal settlements, riverine communities and fast-growing areas,” he said. Mustafa called for stronger primary healthcare financing, investment in frontline health workers and improved access to antenatal care, nutrition counselling, immunisation and birth registration. He also urged journalists to support public health campaigns, counter misinformation and hold government and other stakeholders accountable. “To our friends in the media: you are partners in this work, not spectators,” he said. Also speaking, the Director of Corporate Communications and Corporate Social Responsibility at Airtel Nigeria, Adefemi Adeniran, said a child’s background, economic circumstances or developmental differences should not determine his or her future. “Neither the economic circumstances of a child’s parent, background nor their developmental differences should determine a child’s prospects in life. Keeping them alive is our fundamental obligation. Enabling them to learn is our collective responsibility. Creating conditions for them to thrive must be our shared ambition,” he said. Also the DAME Trustee, Mr. Lanre Idowu, said the partnership between UNICEF, NGE and DAME was helping to strengthen child-rights journalism through training, access to credible evidence, field visits and recognition of excellent reporting. On his part, UNICEF Nigeria Goodwill Ambassador and musician, Cobhams Asuquo, highlighted the role of music in communicating messages about child survival and development. “Music is a powerful tool. It can take an important message beyond the statistics and help people connect with the real lives and experiences behind it. With the First 1,000 Days of Life song, we wanted families and communities to understand that what we do for a child from the very beginning, the nutrition, care and support we provide, can shape that child’s future,” he said. Children also participated in the discussions, questioning decision-makers on how they would ensure that poverty, gender, disability and family circumstances did not deny any child access to healthcare, education and protection. Their performances, including “The First 1,000 Days of Life” and “I Am a Nigerian Child,” reinforced the importance of including children’s voices in decisions affecting their future. The symposium coincided with UNICEF’s 80th anniversary, with participants renewing calls for sustained government leadership, adequate financing, private sector investment, community participation and media accountability to secure a better future for Nigerian children. item.title: 2027: Opposition alliances ‘ll fail again, Fashola declares at APC Lagos rally
item.description: AHEAD of 2027 general elections, former Governor of Lagos State and former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has declared that emerging opposition coalitions will suffer the same fate as past failed alliances in Nigeria’s political history. ​Fashola made the assertion yesterday while speaking as the Chief Host at the Babatunde Raji Fashola, BRF Support Group (BRFSG) Campaign kick-off rally, held at the National Stadium in Surulere, Lagos, where he also launched a grassroots mobilisation drive aimed at building a 10,000-strong volunteer base to secure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the election of Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, as the state’s next governor scheduled for January 16 and February 6, 2027, respectively. The initiative is designed to establish a volunteer-based mobilisation structure across communities, markets, streets and households ahead of the presidential and governorship elections ​ Contrasting the APC 2013 political merger with ongoing talks among rival parties, Fashola, addressing the mammoth crowd of party stalwarts, former heads of service, lawmakers, and students in Lagos, maintained that historical coalitions in 1964, 1983, and 1999 all collapsed without winning the presidency. He dismissed critics who once labeled the APC’s founding blocs as “strange bedfellows,” noting that while the ruling party has consolidated, the opposition has fragmented. ​ “This APC was and remains the only merger that has happened in the history of Nigeria’s political parliament. All of the alliances you have seen on the horizon now will fail too, with your votes,” Fashola told the gathering.Those who see conflict in their party and run away, don’t trust them. They will leave you when things are tough.They don’t stand for anything; they will fall for everything,” he warned. ​​“The intention is to achieve a volunteer party base of 10,000 people, working from now all through to election day, knocking doors, carrying the message of our party, explaining what our party has done, explaining what the candidates have done, explaining what the government has done,” Fashola stated. ​ ​Highlighting the APC’s track record in governance, Fashola pointed to major infrastructure milestones, including: the Lekki Deep Sea Port, the Second Niger Bridge, the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, and the Lagos-Ibadan Railway, as proof of the party’s commitment to long-term economic growth over short-term savings. He emphasized that the upcoming polls are consequential for both Lagos State and Nigeria’s ongoing economic reforms. ​ Taking a swipe at rival political parties, Hamzat accused opposition figures of peddling falsehoods and backtracking on policies they once championed, specifically referencing the removal of the fuel subsidy. Equipping party faithful for door-to-door campaigns, Hamzat outlined key achievements of the Babajide Sanwo-Olu administration and President Tinubu’s federal government, noting that Lagos has domesticated the Electricity Act signed by President Tinubu, enabling the state to participate in power generation, transmission, and distribution. ​Expressing concern over low voter turnout in previous cycles, Hamzat challenged residents to match the state’s high voter registration numbers at the ballot box. item.title: Stay away from our state, Imo APC tells Wike
item.description: The All Progressives Congress, APC, in Imo State, has declared that the state is not available for political manipulation or interference by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike. Read Also: ‘I’m done with Rivers, FCT; give me Imo, Kwara to deliver’ – Wike tells Tinubu It vowed to resist any attempt to import what it described as his controversial political tactics into the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party made its position known in a statement yesterday by its State Publicity Secretary, Onwuasoanya Jones in reaction to alleged Wike’s recent claim that he had concluded arrangements to secure electoral victories for President Bola Tinubu and the APC in the forthcoming elections. Wike was also reported to have offered to undertake additional political assignments for the President, including delivering other states for the APC. Reacting, the Imo APC dismissed the minister’s claims, contending that he should not assume that his political activities could determine the electoral fortunes of the party in different states. The statement particularly faulted Wike for reportedly suggesting that Imo State and another APC-controlled state had political problems requiring his intervention. “We would have ignored the politically displaced errand boy, like we always do, but for the fact that we deem this particular statement of his a direct affront on the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the electoral integrity of our dear party, the APC,” the statement declared. The party accused the FCT minister of attempting to portray President Tinubu as politically dependent on individuals outside the APC to secure electoral victories, insisting that the party enjoys its own grassroots support and political structure. It also faulted Wike’s reported assertion that he had already secured victory for the APC in the FCT and Rivers State, describing such declarations, made weeks before the elections, as disrespectful to democratic principles and the electorate. According to the statement, “our party, the All Progressives Congress, has immense regard for the Nigerian people and would not encourage actions and utterances that tend to cast the Nigerian electorate as irrelevant in the determination of their political future.” The Imo APC further accused Wike of taking advantage of the party’s political goodwill to sustain his relevance while allegedly making disparaging remarks about some of its leaders. It challenged the minister to demonstrate his political influence by campaigning for his own party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), rather than making claims about delivering APC victories. On the political situation in Imo State, the party maintained that its activities were progressing without difficulty and expressed confidence in its preparations for the 2027 elections. It said its mobilisation efforts across the state were ongoing, adding that it expected Imo voters to participate in the forthcoming elections

item.title: Security chiefs hail IGP Disu for suspending declaration of Obaigbena, others wanted
item.description: By Emma Nnadozie THE police order suspending the wanted declaration on Arise TV owner, Mr. Nduka Obaigbena and seven others over alleged assassination attempt by Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Olohundare Jimoh, has elicited reactions from some security chiefs in the country, who said that the wanted declaration was done without due process. One of the security chiefs who spoke with Vanguard, said: “It was misappropriate and procedurally flawed” and showered encomiums on the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, for his quick response by suspending the wanted declaration The Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Zone 2, Onikan, Lagos, Olohundare Jimoh, last Tuesday, declared Chairman of Arise News and This Day Media Group, Chief Nduka Obaigbena, Managing Director of Nestoil, Dr. Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi, and seven others wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank Managing Director, Olusegun Alebiosu in a crowed press conference in Lagos. He said the declaration followed an investigation into the delivery of a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition to Alebiosu’s residence in Lagos. However, in a swift reaction two days later, the IGP, through the Force Public Relations Officer, FPRO, Ani Iniedu suspended the wanted declaration against the suspects and stated that the case has been transferred to the Force Intelligence Department, FID, Abuja, for a thorough and impartial investigation. He also directed the nine individuals to report to the FID, at the Force headquarters , Abuja, between November 26 and 30, 2026. In his reaction, the Director-General of the Institute of Security, Nigeria at the University of Lagos, Mr. Adebayo Akinade, said that the Zone 2 declaration was “misappropriate and procedurally flawed. The IGP’s suspension and transfer to Force Intelligence Department was correct, strategic and has restored public confidence.” Former Director with the Department of State Service, DSS, and currently a security consultant, Mr. Mike Ejiofor, said: “The IGP has the superior order on such matters. When a subordinate makes a mistake, the IGP is in a position to correct it. So, I do not see any conflict in the matter.” In his response the Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of Perfect Security Services Limited, Dr. Patrick Uwagbale saw the incident as “part of a system that is not in order. A good society will do something according to the rules. Even if the allegation is true or not, it is unheard of that someone as IGP would be on seat and a subordinate had the audacity to take such a decision on such a high profile incident without authorisation from the IGP who ordinarily should have the last say on such a matter. This type of behaviour clearly shows that our system is not healthy. “Something is wrong somewhere. There is a gap somewhere. I wholly support the decision of the IGP to suspend the declaration by his subordinate.” Recall also that The Chairman of This Day Newspapers and Arise, Nduka Obaigbena

item.title: 2027 Elections: INEC raises alarm, warns violence may hurt polls
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri and Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, yesterday, warned that the raging waves of political violence could harm the 2027 general elections. Listing Lagos, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Ebonyi, Delta, Cross River, Oyo and Benue as states where incidents of political violence had been recorded, he warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation and the use of thugs, saying such activities could discourage voter participation and undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections. He also cautioned political parties against signing peace accords in Abuja while allegedly sponsoring violence in states, insisting that no political ambition was worth the blood of Nigerians. According to him, attacks have targeted campaign convoys, town hall meetings, party offices and supporters, while INEC officials, staff and ad hoc personnel have also suffered harassment, intimidation and physical attacks by supporters and agents of political parties, both within Nigeria and abroad. It also said it was working with closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. The warning came as INEC and security agencies met in Abuja to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 polls. This came as the Federal Government assured voters, politicians, electoral officials and political parties of protection before, during and after the elections. Speaking at a Strategic Election Security Conference jointly convened by INEC and the Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA, Amupitan said Nigeria had witnessed a disturbing escalation in political intolerance, inflammatory rhetoric and coordinated attacks since the commencement of campaigns in August 2026. Addressing political parties, he said: “Signing peace accords in Abuja while tolerating or financing thuggery in the states is a contradiction our democracy can no longer afford.” He warned that INEC would not succumb to threats or intimidation. “We will neither be intimidated nor blackmailed into compromising our neutrality, and every attack on INEC personnel, facilities, or materials will be met with the full weight of the law,” INEC chairman said. Amupitan said responsibility for electoral violence extended beyond those directly involved in attacks, stressing that political party leaders must be held accountable for the conduct of their candidates and supporters. He said: “Accountability does not end with the foot soldiers who throw stones or wield weapons,” adding that “party leadership bears moral and political responsibility for the conduct of its candidates, campaign councils, and youth wings”. Violence may suppress voter turnout The INEC chairman identified three major consequences of political violence for the electoral process, including voter suppression, threats to the safety of electoral personnel and the possibility of post-election violence. On voter suppression, he said: “When bullets replace ballots and rallies end in bloodshed, ordinary citizens stay home, effectively disenfranchising millions of peaceful Nigerians.” He said the second concern was the safety of more than 1.41 million ad hoc personnel, most of them National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members, to be deployed across 177,299 polling units. “No parent or institution will willingly deploy young Nigerians into environments where political thugs operate with impunity,” he said. On the third consequence, Amupitan warned that violence before elections could create an atmosphere of hostility and rejection after the announcement of results. “Pre-election violence conditions the political climate for post-election rejection,” he said, warning that collation centres could become flashpoints. He said the need to get elections right in Nigeria is because of the regional implications. The country accounts for more than half of West Africa’s population. A peaceful election, he said, would serve as “the primary anchor of regional stability and constitutional order”. Faults arrest provision Turning to enforcement, Amupitan expressed concern over a provision in the Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections, 2026, which allows security agents to arrest electoral offenders only on the instruction of presiding officers or other INEC officials. “This dichotomy has hampered the efficiency of the law enforcement agents to arrest and investigate electoral offenders,” he said. He noted that the same regulations empowered security agencies to prevent violence and activities capable of disrupting elections. The chairman called for the issue to be addressed through a code of conduct and a proposed legal framework for the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, ICCES. He said the Electoral Act 2026 had increased penalties for electoral offences to fines of up to N5 million or 12 months’ imprisonment for individuals, while political parties could face fines of up to N10 million for first breaches. Amupitan added that Section 148 of the Act empowered INEC legal officers and appointed counsel to prosecute electoral offenders directly once case files were transmitted by the police and other relevant agencies. “INEC is fully prepared to discharge its prosecutorial mandate, and our legal teams are ready to review case files from recent violent incidents across the federation,” he said. Amupitan added: “When political actors see prominent sponsors and foot soldiers swiftly arrested, arraigned, and convicted under the 2026 Act, the incentive for violent campaigns will evaporate.” Over 100m verified voters Providing an update on preparations for the elections at the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners, RECs, from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Amupitan said INEC was managing a verified voter register of more than 100 million. He said the commission had removed more than 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System, ABIS, and a statutory claims and objections audit. The exercise reduced the earlier figure of 103 million registered voters to more than 100 million verified records. Amupitan also disclosed that INEC had selected 17,676 polling units for its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, mock accreditation and result upload exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026, ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged security commanders to treat the exercise as a full-scale rehearsal for the elections. The INEC chairman said the presidential and National Assembly elections would hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, while governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections would take place on Saturday, February 6, 2027. FG assures voters, politicians of protection Meanwhile, the National Security Adviser, NSA, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, assured Nigerians that the Federal Government and security agencies would protect voters, politicians, electoral officials and political parties before, during and after the elections. Ribadu, who spoke at the conference, said the administration of President Bola Tinubu was committed to providing the security required for peaceful, transparent and credible elections. “The duty of government and the security agencies is to protect voters, electoral officials and the wider population before, during and after the election. We will protect you. We will protect the voters. We will protect politicians. And even after the election, we will make sure there is no violence,” he declared. He pledged that security agencies would operate impartially and in accordance with the law. “Security agencies will discharge their responsibilities impartially and in accordance with the law,” he said. item.title: The token factory never sleeps
item.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30
item.dc:creator: Robin Birtstone
item.content:encoded: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30 kW. In token factory terms, the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System is the core compute engine. Each system puts eight NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPUs on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, linked by sixth-generation NVLink. ASUS has designed its equipment to support the constraints above. Its customers can choose between the hybrid and fully liquid-cooled models, and they can opt for partial or full rack configurations by buying multiple trays. This enables them to match their facilities' needs. Peak performance versus sustained performance The other difference between model providers and enterprises lies in which numbers they care about. Peak performance is different from sustained performance. The first is a specification sheet number, while the second is what the GPU actually delivers hours into a heavy workload. Production inference tends to run continuously, especially when it uses agents, as opposed to training, which is a sporadic job. So the sustained figure is the one that buyers pay for. Heat becomes a real issue here because when cooling can't keep up, GPUs throttle their clocks to protect themselves. In a token factory, a throttled GPU is a slower production line. The more advanced the architecture becomes, the higher the stakes get. NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU has raised them to their highest point, delivering up to 400 petaflops of NVFP4 inference per eight-GPU board, according to NVIDIA's sparse specification. This is screamingly fast, but the increased heat per board means less margin before throttling. ASUS designed both models to put direct-to-chip liquid cooling on every GPU. Only the 3U unit leaves the CPUs on air cooling. ASUS also says it puts every configuration through a 168-hour stress test. Power and heat set the shape of the rack As boards increase their compute density, pushing up the power and heat requirements, planning naturally has to move out of the server room and into the facility. That's the case whether you're talking about an entire NVL72 rack or a stack of eight-GPU servers like the ASUS systems. There are other things to consider beyond heat. Few datacenters run racks drawing more than 30 kilowatts, says th e Uptime Institute . Yet a single liquid-cooled tray of the ASUS systems draws up to 23.9 kilowatts, and a full rack of nine has a power budget of about 216 kilowatts. Floor loading and power distribution matter as much as cooling. NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU raises the stakes again. The eight-GPU format enables organizations to buy their computing power in more granular steps. That's where the two ASUS systems come into their own. With few enterprises needing a training cluster at NVL72 scale, the advantage is that an HGX box lets them buy AI compute in digestible pieces. The ASUS systems also come with a 54V busbar and cable-free board-to-board design. ASUS says this simplifies assembly and improves reliability. Connectivity, storage and management So that's space, power and heat. But a GPU board won't produce many tokens if the network, storage or operational tooling can't feed it properly. Agent workloads move context and data all the time, so east-west bandwidth and local storage are key to effective utilization. Any new equipment should ideally slot straight into the enterprise's existing management and monitoring tooling. ASUS ships the whole rack, including servers, networking, power and storage, as a single blueprint. ASUS pre-validates this AI Factory reference architecture at rack scale so that organizations can plan for future growth. That includes dedicated management nodes and a management switch. Inside each tray, ASUS has sized the data paths to keep the GPUs fed. Eight OSFP ports on NVIDIA ConnectX-9 give every GPU 800Gb/s of east-west bandwidth to the rest of the cluster, and an NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU adds two 400GbE ports. Within the board, the eight GPUs talk to each other over NVLink at 3,600GB/s, ASUS says. The 2U tray takes up to 4TB of DDR5 system memory and has eight E1.S NVMe bays for fast local data access, while the 3U model offers a choice of U.2 or E1.S drives. Built to be serviced The other issue for enterprises putting AI inference into production is service and maintenance. In a liquid-cooled box, routine fixes can mean draining a coolant loop, which is downtime, and lost token output, that most enterprises can't afford, especially when dealing with non-batch workloads such as inferencing. So ASUS set out to make components quicker to swap. On the 2U fully liquid-cooled model, ASUS did it with independent, tool-less CPU and GPU sleds, each with its own direct-to-chip cooling. On the 3U hybrid, ASUS says the air-cooled CPU sled cuts maintenance time by up to 50 percent. From loading dock to first token Services aren't just about server maintenance. They're also about decreasing the time to value for AI. Most enterprises won't have in-house rack-scale GPU integration skills, which is why pre-validation and design services are so important.

item.title: PDP will reclaim Ebonyi in 2027, chairman declares
item.description: …As Odii receives flag, promises economic revival By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara, has expressed confidence that the party will reclaim Ebonyi State in the 2027 governorship election through its candidate, Chief Ifeanyichukwu Odii. Mohammed stated this in Abakaliki during the campaign flag-off and presentation of flags to Odii and other PDP candidates in the state. He said Ebonyi had remained a PDP stronghold since 1999 until the party lost power, alleging that its mandate was taken away by the ruling party. The national chairman further alleged that the PDP won the last governorship election in the state but was denied victory, insisting that the party would reclaim its mandate in 2027. He urged residents to vote for PDP candidates, saying the party was determined to change the state’s economic fortunes. In his acceptance speech after receiving the party’s flag, Odii criticised Governor Francis Nwifuru’s spending priorities and promised to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, agriculture and infrastructure development if elected. The PDP candidate accused the Nwifuru administration of failing to translate increased federal allocations into improved living conditions for residents. He said that despite the increase in federal allocations to the state since 2023, poverty, inadequate electricity, poor healthcare, sanitation challenges and limited economic opportunities remained major concerns. Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, he said, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty. He also questioned the government’s expenditure priorities, alleging that it spent N19.78 billion on donations, entertainment and refreshments by the third quarter of 2026, while allocating N9 billion to education and healthcare combined. He further alleged that the government spent less than its approved healthcare budget in 2025, while no expenditure was recorded for textbooks and teacher training. He also claimed that agriculture received less than two per cent of the state’s 2025 budget. The businessman said his experience in business and philanthropy had prepared him for the task of governing the state. He said his foundation had built more than 150 homes for less privileged families, awarded scholarships to over 2,500 Nigerians and provided relief materials to more than 40,000 families. According to him, the foundation also supports over 1,000 farmers annually with agricultural inputs and has empowered 3,000 entrepreneurs through grants and seed capital, in addition to executing rural electrification and road projects. Unveiling his development agenda, Odii promised to promote agricultural mechanisation, irrigation, access to finance and agro-processing facilities to improve farmers’ productivity and earnings. He urged residents to vote for PDP candidates, saying the party was determined to change the state’s economic fortunes. In his acceptance speech after receiving the party’s flag, Odii criticised Governor Francis Nwifuru’s spending priorities and promised to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, agriculture and infrastructure development if elected. The PDP candidate accused the Nwifuru administration of failing to translate increased federal allocations into improved living conditions for residents. He said that despite the increase in federal allocations to the state since 2023, poverty, inadequate electricity, poor healthcare, sanitation challenges and limited economic opportunities remained major concerns. Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, he said, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty. He also questioned the government’s expenditure priorities, alleging that it spent N19.78 billion on donations, entertainment and refreshments by the third quarter of 2026, while allocating N9 billion to education and healthcare combined. He further alleged that the government spent less than its approved healthcare budget in 2025, while no expenditure was recorded for textbooks and teacher training. He also claimed that agriculture received less than two per cent of the state’s 2025 budget. The businessman said his experience in business and philanthropy had prepared him for the task of governing the state. He said his foundation had built more than 150 homes for less privileged families, awarded scholarships to over 2,500 Nigerians and provided relief materials to more than 40,000 families. According to him, the foundation also supports over 1,000 farmers annually with agricultural inputs and has empowered 3,000 entrepreneurs through grants and seed capital, in addition to executing rural electrification and road projects. Unveiling his development agenda, Odii promised to promote agricultural mechanisation, irrigation, access to finance and agro-processing facilities to improve farmers’ productivity and earnings. He said his administration would pursue an integrated infrastructure programme covering roads, electricity, water, housing and digital connectivity, while encouraging private-sector investment in power generation and renewable energy. The PDP candidate also promised to improve school infrastructure, strengthen teacher development, expand technical and vocational education and promote youth entrepreneurship. On healthcare, he pledged to equip primary healthcare centres, provide essential medicines and recruit qualified medical personnel, particularly in underserved communities. Odii also promised reforms in the civil service, land administration and justice system, as well as improved security coordination and mechanisms for resolving communal disputes. He said his administration would establish delivery units to monitor projects, introduce periodic performance assessments for ministries, departments and agencies, and publish regular reports on government performance. Earlier, Mohammed urged residents to vote for PDP candidates in the National Assembly elections scheduled for January 16, 2027, and support Odii and other party candidates in the governorship and State Assembly elections on February 6. He expressed confidence that the party would reclaim the state, saying, “History will repeat itself in Ebonyi State come February 6.” The PDP chairman urged residents to mobilise support for the party’s candidates in the Senate and House of Representatives elections, describing the PDP as a party that understood the needs and aspirations of the people. Mohammed commended the party’s leadership for providing a platform to strengthen its political activities in the state, particularly acknowledging the role of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike. He described the reception accorded the party at the campaign flag-off as evidence of its continued strength in Ebonyi. The national chairman expressed optimism that the PDP would win the governorship election, promising that the party’s national leadership would return to the state to celebrate its victory. item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. item.title: Kitto violence: Majority of victims suffer in silence – ISHRAI warns
item.description: .. Only 28% of victims report attacks, survey across six South-West states reveals By Chioma Obinna A growing pattern of online deception, blackmail, sexual exploitation and extortion is exposing young Nigerians and other vulnerable people to physical attacks, psychological trauma and even death, with a survey revealing that 71.3 per cent of respondents across six South-West states had experienced Kitto-related violence. The survey also revealed that only 28 per cent of those affected reported their experiences, highlighting the extent of underreporting and the fear, stigma and discrimination that prevent victims from seeking help. The Improved Sexual Health and Rights Advocacy Initiative (ISHRAI), which disclosed the findings, raised the alarm over the trend, warning that victims were increasingly exposed to kidnapping, sexual abuse, blackmail, mob attacks and other forms of violence. The organisation called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, women and youth groups to intensify community awareness, protect vulnerable people and discourage public shaming, discrimination and jungle justice. Speaking at a stakeholders’ engagement involving traditional and religious leaders, ISHRAI’s Programme Manager, Mrs Sophia Lawal, said community leaders must be equipped with the knowledge and referral mechanisms to identify cases of Kitto-related violence and respond appropriately. Lawal said the engagement brought together 20 traditional and religious leaders, including women leaders, to deliberate on the threats facing marginalised people and develop community-based responses. “It’s very important that we have community members, that’s the religious, traditional leaders, and also the women leaders, to have conversations around kitto violence that affects marginalized people in Nigeria,” she said. “And we cannot address these issues without having the right people in the room to deliberate on this matter together so that they are equipped with the right, with the knowledge to actually handle such cases when they are being reported or how to even identify such cases in their immediate community.” Providing details of the survey, an ISHRAI representative said 240 people were interviewed across the six South-West states, with 71.3 per cent indicating that they had experienced Kitto-related violence. He said the organisation’s intervention was aimed at reducing the practice through public education, early identification and effective community response. Explaining how perpetrators operate, he said many exploit social media to establish relationships with unsuspecting young men and women, build their confidence and lure them into physical meetings under false pretences. According to him, victims are sometimes encouraged to travel long distances, with perpetrators offering to pay their transport fares, book hotel accommodation or even arrange flights. However, upon arriving at the agreed locations, some victims reportedly discover that the meetings are traps

item.content:encoded: .. Only 28% of victims report attacks, survey across six South-West states reveals By Chioma Obinna A growing pattern of online deception, blackmail, sexual exploitation and extortion is exposing young Nigerians and other vulnerable people to physical attacks, psychological trauma and even death, with a survey revealing that 71.3 per cent of respondents across six South-West states had experienced Kitto-related violence. The survey also revealed that only 28 per cent of those affected reported their experiences, highlighting the extent of underreporting and the fear, stigma and discrimination that prevent victims from seeking help. The Improved Sexual Health and Rights Advocacy Initiative (ISHRAI), which disclosed the findings, raised the alarm over the trend, warning that victims were increasingly exposed to kidnapping, sexual abuse, blackmail, mob attacks and other forms of violence. The organisation called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, women and youth groups to intensify community awareness, protect vulnerable people and discourage public shaming, discrimination and jungle justice. Speaking at a stakeholders’ engagement involving traditional and religious leaders, ISHRAI’s Programme Manager, Mrs Sophia Lawal, said community leaders must be equipped with the knowledge and referral mechanisms to identify cases of Kitto-related violence and respond appropriately. Lawal said the engagement brought together 20 traditional and religious leaders, including women leaders, to deliberate on the threats facing marginalised people and develop community-based responses. “It’s very important that we have community members, that’s the religious, traditional leaders, and also the women leaders, to have conversations around kitto violence that affects marginalized people in Nigeria,” she said. “And we cannot address these issues without having the right people in the room to deliberate on this matter together so that they are equipped with the right, with the knowledge to actually handle such cases when they are being reported or how to even identify such cases in their immediate community.” Providing details of the survey, an ISHRAI representative said 240 people were interviewed across the six South-West states, with 71.3 per cent indicating that they had experienced Kitto-related violence. He said the organisation’s intervention was aimed at reducing the practice through public education, early identification and effective community response. Explaining how perpetrators operate, he said many exploit social media to establish relationships with unsuspecting young men and women, build their confidence and lure them into physical meetings under false pretences. According to him, victims are sometimes encouraged to travel long distances, with perpetrators offering to pay their transport fares, book hotel accommodation or even arrange flights. However, upon arriving at the agreed locations, some victims reportedly discover that the meetings are traps. Their phones and valuables are seized, while others are kidnapped, sexually assaulted, filmed in compromising situations or threatened with the publication of nude pictures. The images are subsequently used to blackmail victims and extort money from them, often leaving them too ashamed or traumatised to report the incidents to their families or law enforcement agencies. The representative said some victims resorted to stealing and other desperate measures to meet the demands of their blackmailers, while others suffered severe psychological trauma. He also raised concerns over mob attacks and killings arising from rumours and allegations circulated online, warning that innocent people had been attacked or killed without investigations. “We have seen mob violence. We have seen several persons have been killed, some of them innocently. People who are not supposed to be killed are killed,” he said. He urged communities to reject jungle justice and allow law enforcement agencies to investigate allegations and ensure that anyone found culpable was prosecuted in accordance with the law. “Instead of taking laws in your hand, you report to the leaders of the community. The leaders do a follow-up, do their investigation, also using the state machinery, then those that need to be truly punished, let them be punished according to the law of the land, not on the basis of what a group of persons decide at any point.” The organisation also called for the protection of victims’ identities, warning that public exposure, rumour-mongering and stigmatisation could deepen their trauma and discourage others from reporting abuse. On available support, the representative said Lagos State had six sexual assault referral centres where survivors could receive treatment free of charge. He identified the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Response Agency, the Office of the Public Defender and the National Human Rights Commission as other institutions victims could approach for assistance, including legal support. He said ISHRAI would provide the necessary linkages to ensure that victims were referred to appropriate services. Lawal disclosed that the next step would be to establish a referral pathway through a WhatsApp platform involving the participating community leaders, alongside a directory of relevant government agencies and support organisations. She said the initiative would also encourage the leaders to take the message back to their communities and commit themselves to preventing human rights violations. Also speaking, a Health Education Officer with the Lagos State Primary Health Care Board, Lagos State Health District 6, Mrs Rashida Sanni’Afolabi, described the engagement as an important opportunity to strengthen community participation in protecting vulnerable people. She said traditional rulers, religious leaders and ward health committee members were strategically positioned to bridge the gap between communities and the healthcare system because of their closeness to the people. Sanni’Afolabi stressed that victims of sexual violence should not be blamed or subjected to judgment when they seek help. “Take for instance, someone that’s been raped, a lady that’s been raped, we should not start with the question of why were you raped, probably because she didn’t dress well, but we should remember that we need to address the issue first, so that people can feel safer, they will be able to come out and tell us how they feel,” she said. She urged health workers and community stakeholders to incorporate awareness of rights, sexual and gender-based violence and available support services into their engagements, including school health programmes. According to her, addressing such violence requires a holistic approach that considers the physical, mental and emotional wellbeing of affected persons. The stakeholders agreed that closer collaboration among traditional institutions, religious organisations, government agencies and civil society groups would be necessary to strengthen reporting, protect survivors and ensure that allegations of criminal conduct were handled through lawful channels. ISHRAI said it would continue to support community leaders with information and referral services, stressing that public awareness, respect for human dignity and rejection of violence were essential to preventing further victimisation. The post Kitto violence: Majority of victims suffer in silence – ISHRAI warns appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
item.description: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".
