item.title: ‘Sanitation exercise to hold Saturday as scheduled’ – Lagos Govt
item.description: The Lagos State Government has dismissed rumours of a postponement of the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise, confirming that it will hold across the state on Saturday, November 28, 2026. The exercise is scheduled to take place between 6:30am and 8:30am and will be monitored by government officials across various local government areas and local council development areas. The state government made the clarification on Thursday in a statement signed by Kunle Adeshina, Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources. The statement quoted the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen, as saying there was no basis for postponing the exercise. “There is no basis to cancel the monthly exercise which has become a rallying point for everyone to stay back and clean their neighbourhood,” Tajudeen said. He added that the November edition would be monitored across the state, as had become a tradition. According to the statement, the First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, will lead a team of government officials to monitor the exercise in Eti-Osa Local Government Area. Similarly, another team led by the Head of Service, Mr Olabode Agoro, will monitor activities in Coker-Aguda Local Council Development Area. Explaining the timing of the exercise, Tajudeen said the 6:30am to 8:30am schedule would allow residents to participate in the clean-up without disrupting other activities. He said the timeframe “gives enough room for any form of civic exercise to still be undertaken after the clean-up.” The permanent secretary urged Lagos residents to remain in their neighbourhoods and participate actively in the exercise. He also called on transport unions to use the opportunity to clean their parks and garages before resuming passenger operations at 8:30am. The state government reiterated its call for collective participation in maintaining environmental cleanliness across Lagos State. Vanguard News The post ‘Sanitation exercise to hold Saturday as scheduled’ – Lagos Govt appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: RN’s antisemitic past ‘coming back to haunt them’: Will Le Pen ‘distance herself’ from Bardella?
item.description: Could new allegations of antisemitism damage Jordan Bardella’s standing and the far-right National Rally’s electoral prospects? Charli James is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. Smith examines the far-right leader’s continued denials and considers whether Marine Le Pen might eventually distance herself from him. In the meantime, Smith suggests that Bardella needs to “make his mind up” about how to respond to these latest troubling allegations published by Le Monde and Mediapart. “It’s very difficult to deny. Le Monde and Mediapart, certainly Le Monde, wouldn’t be publishing these details if they didn’t have some pretty substantial evidence.” Could this prove to be the Achilles’ heel of a far-right party with its sights set on the second round of the presidential election?

item.title: Ramaphosa hosts Obasanjo, AFC delegation for Africa infrastructure talks
item.description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has met with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo and a delegation from the African Finance Corporation (AFC) to discuss infrastructure development and investment opportunities across the continent. The meeting, held at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, was led by AFC President and Chief Executive Officer, Samaila Zubairu. Discussions focused on the forthcoming Africa We Build Summit, scheduled to take place in Johannesburg from April 28 to 30, 2027. A statement from the presidency reads in part, “The summit is expected to highlight infrastructure development at a time when African countries are pursuing an ambitious pipeline of cross-border projects aimed at strengthening regional connectivity and economic integration. “Through the Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA), 69 priority projects are currently at various stages of implementation across the continent. However, advancing the projects requires sustainable and predictable financing, alongside stronger partnerships between governments, development finance institutions and private investors.” The discussions between Ramaphosa, Obasanjo and the AFC delegation underscored the importance of mobilising investment and strengthening cooperation to translate Africa’s infrastructure ambitions into tangible development outcomes. The Africa We Build Summit is expected to provide a platform for stakeholders to explore financing opportunities, strengthen partnerships and accelerate the delivery of critical infrastructure projects across the continent. The post Ramaphosa hosts Obasanjo, AFC delegation for Africa infrastructure talks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Is Spain's snap election being rigged? Debunking viral claims
item.description: Ahead of Spain's snap election on Sunday, allegations of vote rigging - known in Spanish as "pucherazo" - are spreading widely on social media. From claims that undocumented migrants are being illegally registered to vote, to allegations that postal ballots and vote counts could be manipulated, internet users are accusing Pedro Sánchez's government of attempting to rig the election. But these claims misrepresent how Spain's electoral system works, as Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

item.title: 'Citizens angry with the establishment' as Spain heads to the polls
item.description: Three party leaders are vying in Spain's general election on Sunday, which leftist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called following a parliamentary setback over housing legislation that underscored the fragility of his minority coalition government. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Policy Centre, says that despite solid economic growth in Spain the population "have suffered a housing crisis and inflation, citizens are still angry with the government and the economic system regardless of macroeconomic data", adding that "in the end citizens are angry with the establishment, in this case it will be Sanchez, but to be honest I think they will be angry at PP and Vox very soon".

item.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
item.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

item.title: 2027: Ebonyi CP warns parties against electoral violence
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police, Hope Urunwa Okafor, has warned political parties and their leaders against violence, thuggery and hate speech ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okafor gave the warning during a meeting she convened with leaders and representatives of political parties in the state to discuss strategies for ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the elections. The meeting was attended by representatives of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party. The police commissioner reiterated that the Nigeria Police Force remained apolitical and impartial in the discharge of its duties. She assured the party leaders that the command was prepared to provide adequate security for campaign activities, protect lives and property, and maintain law and order across the state. Okafor stressed that no society could thrive in an atmosphere of violence, urging political parties to avoid inflammatory rhetoric, hate speech, personal attacks and other forms of communication capable of inciting violence. She charged party leaders to demonstrate responsible leadership by ensuring that their words and actions promoted peaceful political engagement. The commissioner also urged them to demonstrate zero tolerance for violence among their supporters, rather than merely preaching peace. She called on the political parties to exercise restraint in their public statements and campaign activities and provide the command with timely information on their campaign schedules and other political engagements to enable adequate security arrangements. In their separate remarks, the party representatives commended the commissioner for convening the meeting, describing it as timely and necessary ahead of the 2027 elections. They appealed to the police command to provide adequate security during campaigns and other political activities. The party representatives also requested that candidates contesting various elective positions be invited to similar engagements to strengthen collective efforts towards peaceful elections. The post 2027: Ebonyi CP warns parties against electoral violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. item.title: PDP vows to reclaim Ebonyi in 2027
item.description: ..Odii receives party flag, promises economic revival By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara, has expressed confidence that the party will reclaim Ebonyi State in the 2027 governorship election through its candidate, Chief Ifeanyichukwuma Odii. Mohammed stated this in Abakaliki during the party’s campaign flag-off and presentation of flags to Odii and other PDP candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said Ebonyi had remained a PDP-controlled state since 1999 until the party lost power, alleging that its mandate was taken away by the ruling party. The PDP chairman further claimed that the party won the last governorship election in the state but was denied victory, insisting that it would recover its mandate in 2027. He appealed to residents to vote massively for the PDP to change the state’s economic fortunes. Speaking after receiving the party’s flag, Odii criticised Governor Francis Nwifuru’s spending priorities and promised to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, agriculture and infrastructure development if elected. The governorship candidate accused the Nwifuru administration of failing to translate increased federal allocations into improved living conditions for residents. He said despite the increase in federal allocations to the state since 2023, poverty, inadequate electricity, poor healthcare, sanitation challenges and limited economic opportunities remained major concerns. Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, according to him, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty. He also questioned the state government’s expenditure priorities, alleging that it spent N19.78 billion on donations, entertainment and refreshments by the third quarter of 2026, while allocating N9 billion to education and healthcare combined. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: ..Odii receives party flag, promises economic revival By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara, has expressed confidence that the party will reclaim Ebonyi State in the 2027 governorship election through its candidate, Chief Ifeanyichukwuma Odii. Mohammed stated this in Abakaliki during the party’s campaign flag-off and presentation of flags to Odii and other PDP candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said Ebonyi had remained a PDP-controlled state since 1999 until the party lost power, alleging that its mandate was taken away by the ruling party. The PDP chairman further claimed that the party won the last governorship election in the state but was denied victory, insisting that it would recover its mandate in 2027. He appealed to residents to vote massively for the PDP to change the state’s economic fortunes. Speaking after receiving the party’s flag, Odii criticised Governor Francis Nwifuru’s spending priorities and promised to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, agriculture and infrastructure development if elected. The governorship candidate accused the Nwifuru administration of failing to translate increased federal allocations into improved living conditions for residents. He said despite the increase in federal allocations to the state since 2023, poverty, inadequate electricity, poor healthcare, sanitation challenges and limited economic opportunities remained major concerns. Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, according to him, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty. He also questioned the state government’s expenditure priorities, alleging that it spent N19.78 billion on donations, entertainment and refreshments by the third quarter of 2026, while allocating N9 billion to education and healthcare combined. He further alleged that the government spent below its approved healthcare budget in 2025, while no expenditure was recorded for textbooks and teacher training. He also claimed that agriculture received less than two per cent of the state’s 2025 budget. The businessman said his experience in business and philanthropy had prepared him for the task of governing the state. He disclosed that his foundation had built more than 150 homes for less privileged families, awarded scholarships to over 2,500 Nigerians and provided relief materials to more than 40,000 families. According to him, the foundation has also supported over 1,000 farmers annually with agricultural inputs and empowered 3,000 entrepreneurs through grants and seed capital, alongside rural electrification and road projects. Unveiling his development agenda, Odii promised to promote agricultural mechanisation, irrigation, access to finance and agro-processing facilities to improve farmers’ productivity and earnings. He said his administration would pursue an integrated infrastructure programme covering roads, electricity, water, housing and digital connectivity, while encouraging private sector investment in power generation and renewable energy. On education, he promised to improve school infrastructure, strengthen teacher development, expand technical and vocational education and promote youth entrepreneurship. He also pledged to equip primary healthcare centres, provide essential medicines and recruit qualified medical personnel, particularly in underserved communities. Odii further promised reforms in the civil service, land administration and justice system, as well as stronger security coordination and mechanisms for resolving communal disputes. To ensure accountability, he said his administration would establish delivery units to monitor projects, introduce periodic performance assessments for ministries, departments and agencies, and publish regular reports on government performance. Earlier, Mohammed expressed confidence that the PDP would win the 2027 governorship election, urging residents to support the party’s candidates in the National Assembly, governorship and State Assembly elections. He called on the electorate to vote for PDP candidates in the National Assembly elections scheduled for January 16, 2027, and support Odii and other State Assembly candidates on February 6. “History will repeat itself in Ebonyi State come February 6. I want to use this opportunity to call on all the people of Ebonyi. We have candidates for Senate and House of Representatives. Please, on January 16, come out in your numbers and vote for our candidates,” he said. He urged residents to mobilise support for Odii and other PDP candidates, describing the party as one that understood the needs and aspirations of the people. The PDP chairman commended the party’s leadership for providing a platform to strengthen its political activities in the state, particularly acknowledging the role of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike. He described the reception accorded the party during the campaign flag-off as evidence of its continued strength in Ebonyi. Mohammed expressed optimism that the party would emerge victorious in the governorship election, promising that the national leadership would return to the state to celebrate its victory. He urged residents to vote for Odii on February 6, 2027, to ensure the emergence of a PDP government in the state. The post PDP vows to reclaim Ebonyi in 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Messi, Ronaldo could play together for first time at Tevez testimonial
item.description: Former Argentina striker Carlos Tevez said Thursday Lionel Messi would appear in his testimonial next month and that he was confident Cristiano Ronaldo would be playing alongside them. The 42-year-old Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and also lined up with Ronaldo at Manchester United. Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires. Messi, 39, and 41-year-old Ronaldo have faced off against each other many times on the pitch, notably in several El Clasico fixtures during their respective times at Barcelona and Real Madrid. If Tevez succeeds in luring the Portuguese forward to the Bombonera, it could be the first time ever that the pair who marked their generation play on the same side. Other illustrious footballers scheduled for the match are the Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, Argentine midfielder Juan Roman Riquelme and former England centre-back Rio Ferdinand. The post Messi, Ronaldo could play together for first time at Tevez testimonial appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Ogun ADC accepts Supreme Court ruling, backs Ogundipe as guber candidate
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accepted the Supreme Court ruling affirming Biodun Collins Ogundipe, popularly known as BCO, as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections. The party also called on aggrieved members to close ranks and work together for the success of the party at the polls. The decision was taken at a special meeting of the State Executive Committee, local government area (LGA) chairmen, party leaders, elders and other stakeholders held on Thursday. The meeting, presided over by the State Chairman, Otunba Olufemi Soluade, considered the Supreme Court judgment alongside a letter dated November 23, 2026, from the party’s National Legal Adviser, which, according to the state chapter, reinforced the need for the party to operate within the provisions of the law. In a communiqué issued at the end of the meeting, the Ogun ADC said it had resolved to accept the apex court’s decision without prejudice and recognise Ogundipe as the party’s duly affirmed governorship candidate in the state. The party described its position as a demonstration of respect for the rule of law and the need to preserve the party’s unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. The development is expected to provide a fresh direction for the party’s preparations in Ogun State, particularly against the backdrop of leadership and governorship candidacy disputes that had generated disagreements among members. The communiqué further disclosed that Otunba Jimi Adebisi Lawal (JAL) and members of his campaign council had pledged their commitment to supporting the ADC’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, as well as all the party’s candidates in Ogun State. According to the communiqué, the party leadership has resolved to mobilise its entire political structure across the state to ensure victory for its candidates in the forthcoming elections. It said the mobilisation drive would extend across all levels of the party, including the state, local government, ward and polling unit structures. The party also reaffirmed its commitment to working collectively for the success of its candidates contesting the presidential, governorship, senatorial, Federal House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections. It added that political activities would be intensified in the months ahead to strengthen the party’s grassroots structures, expand its support base and consolidate its electoral prospects ahead of 2027. Speaking on the need for reconciliation, Soluade appealed to party members, leaders and stakeholders to put aside their differences and unite behind the party’s collective ambition. He urged party loyalists and political stakeholders to shun bickering, divisive tendencies and unnecessary internal disagreements, emphasising that unity and cooperation were essential to the ADC’s success. item.title: Every smart telescope we've reviewed and highly rate that is cheaper for Black Friday — full list
item.description:
Harry joined Space.com in December 2024 as an e-commerce staff writer covering cameras, optics, and skywatching content. Based in the UK, Harry graduated in 2019 with a Bachelor's degree in American Literature with Creative Writing from the University of East Anglia. A keen photographer, Harry has strong experience with astrophotography and has captured celestial objects with a range of cameras. As a lifelong skywatcher, Harry remembers watching the Perseid meteor shower every summer in his hometown and being amazed by the wonders of the night sky.

Smart telescopes automatically go to, focus on and photograph your favorite night sky targets with only a few minutes of setup and the push of a button. item.title: AC Milan rally from two goals down to beat Olympiakos
item.description: Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan, who had lost three of their opening four matches, gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos. Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knock-out phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Joao Silva’s 49th-minute strike. But Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the former Ipswich winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse to equalise in the 63rd minute. Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth, breathing life into the seven-time European champions’ campaign. Belgians Union Saint-Gilloise are fifth in the standings, one point behind Leverkusen, Ferencvaros and Benfica, after preserving their unbeaten record, also coming back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Lech Poznan. – Clashes in Georgia – The Turkish Football Federation condemned “unacceptable” scenes as Georgian police clashed with Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner. The Istanbul team’s game against Hapoel was being played in Batumi due to security reasons. “We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the UEFA Europa League match between our representative Besiktas and Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia,” the club said. A Turkish ministry source said Turkey’s top diplomat, Hakan Fidan, had spoken with his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili. “Officials from the Turkish Embassy in Tbilisi and the Consulate General in Batumi are at the stadium,” the source said. “All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights.” There were also violent clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters during the Ligue 1 club’s 1-0 win in France. Brighton moved second in the Conference League table by swatting aside Universitatea Craiova of Romania 4-0. Ghana international Ibrahim Osman scored his first goals for the high-flying Premier League club with a double, with Maxim De Cuyper and Charalampos Kostoulas also on the scoresheet. Fabian Hurzeler’s side are two points behind leaders Monaco, who edged out Hearts 3-2 at Tynecastle courtesy of Folarin Balogun’s 94th-minute winner. The post AC Milan rally from two goals down to beat Olympiakos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gbajabiamila leads Tinubu’s delegation to IBB, Abdulsalami
item.description: Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, Femi Gbajabiamila, on Thursday led a presidential delegation to Minna, Niger State, to pay courtesy visits to former military Heads of State, Generals Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida and Abdulsalami Abubakar. Gbajabiamila disclosed this in a statement, saying the visit was undertaken at the directive of President Tinubu to convey his goodwill and best wishes to the two elder statesmen. He said the delegation was warmly received by both former leaders, who appeared well and in high spirits during the visits. According to him, Babangida expressed satisfaction with the Tinubu administration’s performance, reaffirmed his support for the President and wished him success. Abdulsalami, on his part, commended the administration’s performance and thanked Tinubu for remembering the former leaders despite the demands of the ongoing election campaign. Gbajabiamila described the two former leaders as important figures in Nigeria’s history, noting that their experience and counsel remained invaluable to the country. “These are men who occupy major chapters in Nigeria’s history and their counsel remains invaluable,” he said. He added that the President was pleased with their support and expressed optimism about their continued backing in the coming elections. The visits come amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties and their candidates intensify consultations and mobilise support across the country. Babangida, who ruled Nigeria from 1985 to 1993, remains one of the country’s most influential former military leaders, while Abdulsalami, who assumed power in June 1998, oversaw the transition programme that ushered in the Fourth Republic in May 1999.

item.title: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a shift in tone towards the leader Russian he called his friend just a week ago. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. The US leader's comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which they issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: Le Pen slams push for EU budget deal before French election
item.description: EU leaders locked horns over the bloc's budget at a summit meeting in Brussels on Thursday, as far-right leader Marine Le Pen slammed an "underhanded" push to lock in the long-term spending plans before French presidential elections next year. European Council head Antonio Costa turned up the pressure upon arrival at the budget talks, where heavyweight Germany is pressing for cuts as well as burden-sharing on money for Ukraine. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

item.description: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.” It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil . Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United , whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. Continue reading...

item.title: Slow internet? The best wifi extenders and mesh systems to boost your home network – tested
item.description: We put 11 range extenders and mesh systems to the test to find the fastest and most reliable for streaming, gaming and working from home • The best office chairs Fast fibre broadband is fantastic – if the wifi signal reaches the part of your home where you need it. Most of us use the router provided by our broadband provider, often tucked away in a hallway or corner of the lounge. Sadly, these often don’t have the range to cover every room in your home, leaving you high and dry when you’re trying to binge-watch TV or get work done in a distant home office. Wifi extenders and mesh systems can help. Extenders plug in to a mains socket between your location and the router, then pass data backwards and forwards to extend your router’s reach. Mesh systems are even smarter, pairing a secondary router with one or two satellite units, which work together to extend the wifi coverage throughout your home. The mesh system can pass your connection from unit to unit to make sure you’re always getting the best possible link from your device to the internet, wherever you are in your home. Continue reading...

item.title: 32 Years Later, Disney's Most Notorious Cash-Grab Sequel Is Better Than You Remember
item.description: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdin titled The Return of Jafar . Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin , Disney made sequels to The Lion King , The Little Mermaid , Pocahontas , Mulan , and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi . These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films .

item.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
item.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and res
item.dc:creator: Connor Jones
item.content:encoded: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and results of actions, and report back to the threat actor." Notably, ARTEX does not offer any new attack techniques. All of the tool's capabilities were previously known to the cybersecurity world, but its value lies in the automation capabilities it offers users, chaining attacks at machine speed. In the UK NCSC's warning about AOFs this week, it said the key strengths of this technology are its speed, its thoroughness in probing target systems for weaknesses, how it learns from failures instantly, and that it is inexpensive to run at scale. AOFs' speed comes at a cost, however. These tools are noisy, the NCSC said, making them easier to detect in network logs and by defensive solutions. Some examples of the attacks in which the tool has been implicated include Storm-0940's hit on ConnectWise, which enabled attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, various financial institutions in South Korea and India , UK registrar 123 Reg , and the European Commission . ®

item.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
item.description: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

item.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
item.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

item.title: Indie web browser Ladybird enters alpha testing
item.description: The independent Ladybird web browser has reached an important milestone: an alpha test version. What's more, it works well. These may not be the criteria by which some will judge it, though. Earlier this week, the developer behind the Ladybird web browser announced that Ladybird is now in alpha . We've given it a brief test, and it performed very well. It's more stable and works better than its alpha label would suggest. There are downloads available , covering macOS on Apple Silicon, as well as for Linux on x86-64; for the latter, there's a Flatpak package, as well as native Ubuntu and Fedora packages. It's an open source project, so you can download the source code from the GitHub repository and compile it yourself, but in an unusual move, back in June the project announced that the developers would no longer accept public code contributions. We first mentioned Ladybird as part of our early 2022 look at its original parent project – SerenityOS: Remarkable project with its own JS-capable web browser . Both the name and the date are significant: the former is a nod to the Serenity prayer , recited at the end of Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. The date of the article is because it's well before the launch of ChatGPT at the end of 2022 . About a year and a half later, we reported that Serenity OS turns five and emits first offspring, Ladybird . Both the OS and the browser were still hand-coded, but now the browser could be compiled and run on other OSes. That freed it up to call upon external libraries which didn't exist for SerenityOS. Earlier this year, we wrote Ladybird flutters toward Rust with a little help from AI . At one point, developer Andreas Kling used Apple's Swift language, but this year, he changed course and adopted Rust instead, using LLM tools to convert some existing code. Some will dismiss Ladybird because of this, but as our first coverage shows, the browser and its original host OS were established projects before the current wave of AI-assisted development. Kling does use LLMs, but Ladybird is not some sloppy vibe-coded effort. The macOS download is 68.4 MB in size, which in 2026 is remarkably small. The Flatpak is larger – about 111 MB – but it also pulls in some KDE dependencies which increase its size. We tested it on Pop!_OS. It handles sites such as The Register and Hacker News and everything else we tried perfectly, and took just 6 percent of our Dell XPS13's CPU to play full-screen HD video from YouTube smoothly. In our short testing, we saw no crashes, hesitation, or any other problems at all. The developers nevertheless warn that the alpha can crash, some websites will not work, and they make no security guarantees at this stage. The use of LLMs will put some people off. However, this is not the only controversial thing about the project. As we have noted in our previous coverage, Ladybird belongs to the same political wing of the FOSS movement as Omarchy, XLibre, and other right-wing projects. If the LLM use doesn't

item.content:encoded: The independent Ladybird web browser has reached an important milestone: an alpha test version. What's more, it works well. These may not be the criteria by which some will judge it, though. Earlier this week, the developer behind the Ladybird web browser announced that Ladybird is now in alpha . We've given it a brief test, and it performed very well. It's more stable and works better than its alpha label would suggest. There are downloads available , covering macOS on Apple Silicon, as well as for Linux on x86-64; for the latter, there's a Flatpak package, as well as native Ubuntu and Fedora packages. It's an open source project, so you can download the source code from the GitHub repository and compile it yourself, but in an unusual move, back in June the project announced that the developers would no longer accept public code contributions. We first mentioned Ladybird as part of our early 2022 look at its original parent project – SerenityOS: Remarkable project with its own JS-capable web browser . Both the name and the date are significant: the former is a nod to the Serenity prayer , recited at the end of Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. The date of the article is because it's well before the launch of ChatGPT at the end of 2022 . About a year and a half later, we reported that Serenity OS turns five and emits first offspring, Ladybird . Both the OS and the browser were still hand-coded, but now the browser could be compiled and run on other OSes. That freed it up to call upon external libraries which didn't exist for SerenityOS. Earlier this year, we wrote Ladybird flutters toward Rust with a little help from AI . At one point, developer Andreas Kling used Apple's Swift language, but this year, he changed course and adopted Rust instead, using LLM tools to convert some existing code. Some will dismiss Ladybird because of this, but as our first coverage shows, the browser and its original host OS were established projects before the current wave of AI-assisted development. Kling does use LLMs, but Ladybird is not some sloppy vibe-coded effort. The macOS download is 68.4 MB in size, which in 2026 is remarkably small. The Flatpak is larger – about 111 MB – but it also pulls in some KDE dependencies which increase its size. We tested it on Pop!_OS. It handles sites such as The Register and Hacker News and everything else we tried perfectly, and took just 6 percent of our Dell XPS13's CPU to play full-screen HD video from YouTube smoothly. In our short testing, we saw no crashes, hesitation, or any other problems at all. The developers nevertheless warn that the alpha can crash, some websites will not work, and they make no security guarantees at this stage. The use of LLMs will put some people off. However, this is not the only controversial thing about the project. As we have noted in our previous coverage, Ladybird belongs to the same political wing of the FOSS movement as Omarchy, XLibre, and other right-wing projects. If the LLM use doesn't put you off, the political views may. On the other hand, as we've seen from our earlier coverage of Omarchy and XLibre, the same factors also attract others. The modern Web is an entire complex compute platform in its own right, and currently, only three tools support it – and two of those are interrelated. The dominant engines are Google's Blink, used by Chrome and other Chromium browsers; Apple's WebKit, used by Safari; and Mozilla's Gecko, used by Firefox. Blink was forked from WebKit. Some day, when the Servo project matures some more, it may be another. Even so, today, the first preliminary release of Ladybird means that there are now four competitive modern browser engines. That's a significant step. ®

item.title: NAF: Tinubu Approves ₦100m, Houses For Families Of Air Crash Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved a monetary compensation of ₦100 million for the families of military personnel and civilians who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The President also approved a three-bedroom flat in Abuja for the families of military personnel and civilians who lost their lives in the air crash. ﻿ President Tinubu gave the approval during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony in honour of the 25 victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. In his address, the President commiserated with the bereaved families, the military and the nation, as he promised better equipment for the military. “It places upon us a sacred duty to safeguard their well-being, strengthen their capabilities and honour their service. As Commander-in-Chief, I reaffirm my administration’s commitment to a professional, well-equipped, and mission-ready Armed Forces. We will continue to prioritise modernisation, training, operational safety, and the welfare of our personnel. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wing it can build. We must also stand by the families who bear the deepest cost of national service. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of a three-bedroom flat in the Renewed Hope housing project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. No home can ever replace the one you have lost. But they gave their lives to Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their families a home. This honour is extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board,” Tinubu said. “In addition to the flats, those officers will receive from this government ₦100 million each to settle their families. I will commit their soul into the massive hands of Almighty God.” The President assured Nigerians that the accident would be thoroughly investigated, adding that his administration will strengthen the military and civilian aviation safety standards. “Your loss is our nation’s loss, and your grief is our grief. They were not merely passengers aboard the aircraft. They were our gallant officers, airmen and airwomen and fellow compatriots who travelled along with them. They were parents who will not see their children grow. They were newlyweds whose marriage and marriages had only just begun. They were sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, husbands, wives and friends,” he said. “They carried dreams in their hearts and our flag on their shoulders. We could not bring them home to you, and our inability to recover their remains has made this harder still. But hear me, the sky did not take their honour. Nothing can diminish the worth of their lives or the love they leave behind. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. item.dc:creator: Alexander Okere
item.content:encoded: President Bola Tinubu has approved a monetary compensation of ₦100 million for the families of military personnel and civilians who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The President also approved a three-bedroom flat in Abuja for the families of military personnel and civilians who lost their lives in the air crash. ﻿ President Tinubu gave the approval during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony in honour of the 25 victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. In his address, the President commiserated with the bereaved families, the military and the nation, as he promised better equipment for the military. “It places upon us a sacred duty to safeguard their well-being, strengthen their capabilities and honour their service. As Commander-in-Chief, I reaffirm my administration’s commitment to a professional, well-equipped, and mission-ready Armed Forces. We will continue to prioritise modernisation, training, operational safety, and the welfare of our personnel. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wing it can build. We must also stand by the families who bear the deepest cost of national service. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of a three-bedroom flat in the Renewed Hope housing project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. No home can ever replace the one you have lost. But they gave their lives to Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their families a home. This honour is extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board,” Tinubu said. “In addition to the flats, those officers will receive from this government ₦100 million each to settle their families. I will commit their soul into the massive hands of Almighty God.” The President assured Nigerians that the accident would be thoroughly investigated, adding that his administration will strengthen the military and civilian aviation safety standards. “Your loss is our nation’s loss, and your grief is our grief. They were not merely passengers aboard the aircraft. They were our gallant officers, airmen and airwomen and fellow compatriots who travelled along with them. They were parents who will not see their children grow. They were newlyweds whose marriage and marriages had only just begun. They were sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, husbands, wives and friends,” he said. “They carried dreams in their hearts and our flag on their shoulders. We could not bring them home to you, and our inability to recover their remains has made this harder still. But hear me, the sky did not take their honour. Nothing can diminish the worth of their lives or the love they leave behind. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. We owe them the truth. And we will honour that debt as we lay this wreath today,” the President added. Tinubu, who arrived at the National Military Cemetery at about 2:20 p.m., accompanied by the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, and other senior government officials, was received by the chief mourner, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Aneke, alongside the service chiefs and the Inspector-General of Police. With him were Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd.), National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, and the Governor of Ondo State, Lucky Aiyedatiwa. Christian and Muslim prayers were offered for the repose of the souls of the departed. The 25 victims were then honoured by name — five crew members and 20 passengers, including 19 military personnel and six civilians. The wreath-laying was led by Tinubu, followed by other dignitaries and representatives of the bereaved families, just as national flags were presented to the next of kin of the deceased. The ceremony ended with volleys by the firing party, the sounding of reveille, and the national anthem, in everlasting memory of the 25 fallen heroes. The aircraft crashed in Igbokoda while on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos. There were no survivors. item.title: The 14 Best Star Wars Games of All Time, Ranked
item.description: Star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982. Since then, the franchise itself has largely matured alongside the medium, encompassing everything from role-playing games and first-person shooters to arcade racers and XCOM clones (the latter of two seeing well-regard releases just this year). No matter the year or the hardware, some of the best Star Wars games are worth revisiting. Here are the 12 best Star Wars games of all time, ranked.

item.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
item.description: Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win . Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41. “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.” The video was directed by Zack Snyder and features Matt Damon’s voice-over. Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura. Read full article Comments

item.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different." "The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. But as they voyage home (geddit?) in a reconditioned Klingon Bird-of-Prey nicknamed the Bounty — complete with a cloaking device that wil

The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. But as they voyage home (geddit?) in a reconditioned Klingon Bird-of-Prey nicknamed the Bounty — complete with a cloaking device that will come in very handy when hiding in Golden Gate Park — they learn that an alien probe of unknown origin (one of the coolest "Star Trek" spaceships ) is tearing Earth apart looking for humpback whales. With the species extinct since the 21st century, the crew travel back in time via one of the most surreal sequences in "Star Trek" history — Morphing CG heads? What the hell was Nimoy thinking? — in the hope of finding the whales that might just be able to ask politely if the probe might leave us alone. (Image credit: Paramount) Screenwriters Steve Meerson and Peter Krikes were assigned to the project early on (working with Nimoy and producer Harve Bennett on the story), and their treatments included a future Earth under threat from a plague and a discarded subplot about Lt. Saavik being pregnant with Spock's child as a result of the pon farr mating ritual. There were also discussions about the Bird-of-Prey decloaking above the Super Bowl, and — most bizarrely of all — a guest-starring role for Eddie Murphy as an astrophysicist who wants to believe in aliens. Murphy was both a Trekkie and one of the biggest stars on the planet at the time but ultimately decided to make notorious stinker "The Golden Child" instead. "In retrospect, I think I might have been better off doing 'Star Trek IV'," he said later. Paramount had also gotten cold feet about putting the star of the highly lucrative "Beverly Hills Cop" in its highest-profile franchise. "Paramount said, 'We're not going to put out [our] two most valuable assets in one movie – so start over, folks!'" said Nicholas Meyer (h/t The Telegraph ), hired to retool the script after Murphy's departure. "That's why I was called at the last minute." (Image credit: Paramount) Meyer was already "Star Trek" royalty, having brought the movie series to life as director and uncredited writer of "The Wrath of Khan". Indeed, he's arguably the reason the "odd numbers bad/even numbers good" theory of "Trek" films persisted for so long, having later gone on to co-write and direct "Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country". He shared scripting duties with Bennett, with the producer writing the 23rd-century-set bookends of the film, and Meyer handling everything in present-day California. Weirdly, Meyer had prior experience bringing a time traveler to contemporary San Francisco in his 1979 HG Wells/Jack the Ripper adventure "Time After Time". With the three previous "Star Trek" movies largely studio-based, "The Voyage Home" marked a rare chance for cast and crew to head out on location. The Monterey Bay Aquarium filled in for the Cetacean Institute (slightly implausible home of humpbacks George and Gracie), while the USS Ranger — moored in San Diego and no stranger to Hollywood after "Top Gun" — guest-starred as a nuclear "wessel". (Image credit: Paramount) Kirk and co. also headed out onto the streets of San Francisco. Nimoy had toyed with giving them '80s-appropriate disguises, but changed his mind when he realized nobody would bat an eyelid at their 23rd-century civilian attire. Aside from some second unit work photographing humpbacks off the coast of Hawaii, the whales themselves were mostly animatronics created by Industrial Light & Magic. "One of the reasons we think that ['The Voyage Home'] really didn't win visual-effects awards is people didn't really understand how good [the whales were]," said executive producer Ralph Winter. "ILM did such a good job on those whales that they went on tour for a year or more around the world to museums because the expertise, the art, and science of what they had done was very good." Meyer, meanwhile, fully embraced the opportunity to write a fish-out-of-water comedy, with this seasoned crew of Starfleet veterans struggling to get their heads around the eccentricities of late 20th-century America. (Image credit: Paramount) Kirk and Spock experiment extensively with "colorful metaphors" — "double dumbass on you!" — while Kirk gets out of paying for dinner by using the convenient excuse that money isn't a thing in the future. Scotty (James Doohan) attempts to talk to a mid-'80s Apple Macintosh via a mouse before he risks screwing with the timeline by 'inventing' transparent aluminum decades early. And in the film's most famous moment, Spock delivers a Vulcan neck pinch to a punk playing his music very loudly on a public bus, winning extensive applause from his fellow passengers in the process. The nuisance rocker was played by Nimoy's assistant, Kirk Thatcher, who co-wrote the "I Hate You" song that plays on that era-authentic ghetto blaster. He later returned to the role in "Star Trek: Picard", though this time he responded more apologetically to Seven of Nine's request to turn it down. Kirk is undoubtedly the center of the movie, pulling the strings and getting his first romantic interest since the Original Series — whale expert Dr Gillian Taylor (Catherine Hicks), who eventually accompanies the Enterprisers back to the fut

item.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
item.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Waka

From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Wakama PR and Communications Associate, M.Inc PR and Ayodele Johnson, Content Executive, M.Inc PR at the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Collaboration as a Driver of Economic Opportunity A stronger credit ecosystem requires collaboration among financial institutions, fintech companies, regulators, investors, businesses and development organisations. Each has a role to play in improving access to reliable information, developing relevant financial solutions and building confidence in the credit system. Emphasising the importance of collective action, Dr. Jameelah Sharrieff-Ayedun , Managing Director/CEO, CreditRegistry, noted that “No single institution can reimagine Africa’s credit economy alone,” highlighting the need for lenders, regulators, policymakers and innovators to work together in advancing the sector. Afreximbank’s position as the Expo’s founding sponsor also reflects the connection between financial infrastructure, trade and enterprise development, particularly as African economies seek to expand opportunities for businesses across the continent. The discussions at ACE 2026 underscored that expanding access to credit across Africa will require more than the availability of capital. Reliable credit information, financial literacy, responsible innovation and collaboration among financial institutions, businesses, policymakers and technology providers will all be critical to building a more inclusive and trusted credit ecosystem. Commenting on the significance of the Expo, Mirabel Emma Aleladia , CEO and Lead Strategist, M.Inc PR, said, “ Africa’s evolving credit economy requires sustained engagement among the organisations, institutions and innovators shaping the financial services landscape. Platforms such as ACE provide an important opportunity to exchange perspectives, examine emerging developments and strengthen the relationships that can contribute to progress across the sector. For M.Inc PR, being part of these conversations also reinforces the importance of understanding the industries and business environments which our clients operate.” M.Inc PR served as the official media partner for the Expo, supporting media visibility for the event and its conversations on the future of Africa’s credit economy. The partnership reflects the agency’s commitment to staying informed about developments across business and financial services, and understanding the issues shaping the organisations and audiences it serves. Through platforms such as ACE, M.Inc continues to broaden its industry perspective and remain connected to conversations influencing Africa’s evolving business landscape.
