item.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
item.description:
Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. item.dc:creator: Alan Bradley
item.content:encoded:
Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. It takes the trickiness of moving on ice in sports like hockey and increases it by several orders of magnitude. Of course, the havoc wouldn't stop with maneuvering yourself. Any ball or other object would also be subject to this altered set of physics. As Johnson points out, "Aside from maneuvering the body and not tumbling or going in the wrong direction, the most difficult part would probably be throwing or hitting a ball in zero g. There would be no arc, just a straight-line throw. That would take getting used to doing, given that we’ve spent our entire lives calculating how high and fast to throw a ball in 1G so it gets to the person we intend." Science fiction interpretations have often leaned into these differences; in many cases, low-g sports look more like three-dimensional chess than the highly physical contests we're used to here on Earth. Zero‑g competition in sci‑fi worlds (Image credit: Lionsgate Films) Ironically, many of the best examples of space-based sports are the most grounded, where real-world physics are fully accounted for. 2013's "Ender's Game" gives us one of the best examples of a zero-g arena in space. Dubbed the "Battle Room," it's a giant hollow cube filled with obstacles. Teams enter through gates at opposite ends and participate in laser tag-style drills while having to grapple with three-dimensional space, while also finding ways to propel and protect themselves. "The Battle Room sequence does a great job of thinking about straight‑line, constant‑velocity motion," Johnson said. "No 'reaction' to slow you down or change your direction. Characters push off walls or each other, then drift until they hit something or fire their suit's thrusters." Johnson said Ender's Game also did an admirable job of showcasing how alternate physics require another layer of planning when moving through space. "They went to great lengths to show that there was no preferred 'up' or 'down'. Again, very accurate and realistic thinking. Floating obstacles in the battle space created realistic constraints: if you don't think about where you'll rebound, you can pin yourself behind an obstacle or drift out of the fight." Real proposals for space sports Visionary artist Pat Rawlings sees the moon's one-sixth gravity as an excellent environment for athletic competitions. (Image credit: NASA/Pat Rawlings) Recognizing how important play can be (and, perhaps, acknowledging ways to combat the lingering specter of space madness ), real-world space agencies have begun brainstorming what recreation in low gravity might look like. Some proposed ideas include 3D ball games not wholly dissimilar from the Battle Room, where players enter a cube or spherical arena and push off walls/pass a ball in any direction, scoring by hitting targets. Elastic tethers are another experimental concept being bandied around, where players are connected to flexible tethers to improve movement control and cut down on collisions. The Space Games Federation has also floated the idea of a version of space basketball , where the goal is guiding a magnetic ball through hoops, as well as some version of space dodgeball. Of course, these proposals are nothing more than thought exercises at the moment. We're a long way out from vast human populations living in zero-g environments for extended periods of time, and even further still from building spaceships capable of housing a sports hall. NASA astronauts have experimented with trying to play various terrestrial sports in space, usually aboard the International Space Station. We've seen them playing soccer , lacrosse , and hockey with varying degrees of success. These fun experiments mainly serve to prove what we've already suspected: that terrestrial sports can't be directly translated into a zero-g environment. We'll need new rules, arenas, and whole new games if we're going to make any headway with competitive sports in space. Where sci‑fi gets it right (and wrong) about space sports (Image credit: Ready at Dawn) Sci-fi has a pretty good track record for simulating open 3D environments in microgravity. The genre also tends to do fairly well in depicting the methodical pace of moving through space and how that would affect competition (and combat). Games like "Echo Arena" even use technology to help simulate these factors. Echo Arena is a VR game where you boost around a zero-g arena, punching opponents and trying to toss a disc into a goal. The game's innovative movement system allows players to grab almost any surface, either moving themselves along it or pushing off to float in a given direction. Players are also given wrist-mounted thrusters to let them course-correct a little, offering a respite from the unforgiving laws of motion. Dead Space also has a section that functions similarly but with conventional game controls, though the only sport there is "don't get eaten by necromorphs." With that said, there are areas where sci-fi portrayals of zero-G games fall down. Energy levels and fatigue is a big one: constant maneuvering with your arms is exhausting, which is why real astronauts rely heavily on handho

item.title: How to Style Green Lace for Asoebi Like Mercy Aigbe
item.description: Structural tailoring meets monochrome colour play in Mercy Aigbe’s olive and sage green asoebi look. Whenever a green dress code lands in your inbox for an upcoming wedding or celebration, the goal is always making the colour feel fresh and flattering rather than predictable. Nollywood star and filmmaker, Mercy Aigbe just gave us the sweetest blueprint for how to wear green lace for asoebi without letting heavy fabric wear you . The secret to nailing monochrome green for asoebi is mixing your shades and textures so you avoid one flat block of colour from head to toe. Mercy’s gown pairs a smooth, velvety olive corset—complete with visible boning and a central trail of beaded leaf appliqués—with a heavily beaded mermaid skirt in the same olive family . Mercy Aigbe showcases the full silhouette of her olive green corset and beaded lace mermaid gown paired with a marbled sage headtie. Keeping the bodice matte while the skirt sparkles lets the silhouette breathe, and crowning the outfit with a lighter, marbled sage headtie (gele) brightens up the face far better than a dark green wrap ever could. When taking your own green lace to the tailor, borrow her structural tricks: an asymmetrical off-the-shoulder neckline with 3D floral cutouts draws the eye upward, while a diagonal beaded sash-peplum along one hip creates curves without adding bulk around your waist. Mercy Aigbe pairs her olive green lace outfit with a deep red crystal crescent clutch and matching red manicure. As for how to accessorise a green monochrome outfit, skip the usual all-gold default and bring in a rich contrast colour. Olive and sage sit right opposite red on the colour wheel, which is why Mercy’s gold jewellery set with dark red stones, crescent red crystal clutch, and glossy red nails pop so well against the green . Paired with warm golden-bronze eyeshadow and a glossy nude-brown lip , the whole look feels balanced, celebratory, and ready for any guest list. Mercy Aigbe pairs her olive green lace outfit with a deep red crystal crescent clutch and matching red manicure. *** Photo Credit: Mercy Aigbe Adeoti/Instagram The post How to Style Green Lace for Asoebi Like Mercy Aigbe appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
item.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. Continue reading...

item.title: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment | Nils Pratley
item.description: Jensen Huang’s return as CEO comes despite fact board hasn’t completed investigation into reports of affair with alleged Chinese spy Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO What was it that Nvidia’s board was saying about there being no chance of Jensen Huang coming back? The position – a mere six days ago – was supposed to be definitive. The exit of the co-founder came after “disclosure of personal behaviour inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards and cultural norms”, said Harvey Jones, who had been rapidly installed as chair of the chipmaker. The board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” after he “voluntarily resigned”, added Jones . Continue reading...

item.title: Temi Nkem, Big Brother Naija 11 Winner, Signs on as Checkers Custard Brand Ambassador
item.description: Official Unveiling of Temi Nkem and Karan Checker Temi Nkem (born Temitope Chigbue ), ultimate finalist of Big Brother Naija Show Ya Sef , the eleventh edition of Africa’s TV game show, added another feather to her cap just weeks after coming out tops at the eleventh edition of the DStv reality show. Checkers Custard , Nigeria’s custard brand, welcomed the starlet as chief brand influencer cum Brand Ambassador at a signing ceremony chaired by Karan Checker , Managing Director, Checkers Africa , at a ceremony witnessed by the media, friends, staff, influencers and a host of well-wishers. It’s a Homecoming! Karan Checker, Temi Nkem and Ashish Checker The entire continent of Africa witnessed the 21-year-old influencer’s genuine love for Checkers Custard during her ten-week stay in Big Brother’s house with the incessant trips to the kitchen primarily to make her favourite snack, in-between meal filler and as a whole meal with select pairings. Checkers Custard was central to her nutritional routine. File signing Temi came home. Temi Nkem x Checkers Custard Temi, at the winning prize presentation a few days after the grand finale, remarked, “ …we use Checkers Custard for our cake and custard in London. When I was telling everybody cake and custard is dessert, they were saying no, it’s breakfast, so I tried it the first time… it was ‘bussing’… I don’t know how to cook… but that one I needed to make sure I made sure I knew how to do, and I am so happy, so grateful” The British-born Nigerian Accounting & Finance undergrad came into the country solely to participate in the fiercely contested game show and excelled week in, week out, showing her prowess in executing a strategy of being herself, showing her resilience and goodly disposition. These traits did not go unnoticed as Checkers Custard’s brand handlers watched keenly, finally determining to welcome home their providence-chosen brand evangelist. A Truly Natural Fit Keran Checker, the Managing Director of Checkers Africa Limited, the parent company of Checkers Custard, at the signing ceremony in his speech said, “ T emi Nkem is one of a kind; she came, she saw, and conquered the world with her charm and exceptional attitude at Big Brother Naija, and this made us take a deep look into the beautiful and interesting young lady and explore the potential of her representing the brand due to shared values and unparalleled natural alignment ”. While noting that not every Checkers Custard lover in Big Brother’s house in the future would automatically merit an ambassadorial appointment with Checkers Custard, and what made Ms. Chigbue different, Head of Marketing, Checkers Africa, Timothy Ogundele said in his closing remarks on her character traits, “ Even with a fiery personality and unapologetic, Temi remained true to her values demonstrating a deep sense of restraint and discipline making her suitable for our brand. ” A Date with Temi Nkem The official signing ceremony event took place at the offices of Chec

These traits did not go unnoticed as Checkers Custard’s brand handlers watched keenly, finally determining to welcome home their providence-chosen brand evangelist. A Truly Natural Fit Keran Checker, the Managing Director of Checkers Africa Limited, the parent company of Checkers Custard, at the signing ceremony in his speech said, “ T emi Nkem is one of a kind; she came, she saw, and conquered the world with her charm and exceptional attitude at Big Brother Naija, and this made us take a deep look into the beautiful and interesting young lady and explore the potential of her representing the brand due to shared values and unparalleled natural alignment ”. While noting that not every Checkers Custard lover in Big Brother’s house in the future would automatically merit an ambassadorial appointment with Checkers Custard, and what made Ms. Chigbue different, Head of Marketing, Checkers Africa, Timothy Ogundele said in his closing remarks on her character traits, “ Even with a fiery personality and unapologetic, Temi remained true to her values demonstrating a deep sense of restraint and discipline making her suitable for our brand. ” A Date with Temi Nkem The official signing ceremony event took place at the offices of Checkers Africa, playing host to the media, content creators, and friends interacting and networking over ample food and drinks and good music. Temi & Karan Checker Honouring her multiple roots, Temi arrived to Ayanjo Dance Troupe performing a Delta dance routine. With beloved household staples such as Checkers Custard, Checkers Pap, Checkers Crunchy Peanuts, and 3-in-1 Checkers ChocoTe e, the company continues to build a legacy of trust and great taste across Africa. Checkers Custard was an associate sponsor of Big Brother Naija 11, Show Ya Sef , their third sponsorship of the game show. Temi Nkem with her Mother and Family. item.title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
item.description: null NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Some of the features are so thin and flat that the mission team likened them to potato chips, according to a statement from the space agency. NASA's Curiosity rover captured a close-up view of unusual, disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in Martian bedrock using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) on Nov. 7, 2026 (Sol 5067). The thin, flattened formations resemble tiny potato chips. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Curiosity used its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), mounted on the end of its robotic arm, to capture detailed close-up images of the formations on Nov. 7 — the rover's 5,067th Martian day , or Sol 5067. The rover also used its ChemCam instrument to study the rocks' chemical composition, while samples from the Nazca drill site were delivered to its onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument for further analysis. Meanwhile, NASA's Perseverance rover has been investigating a collection of unusually bright rocks in an area called "Idubi," located in the “Lac de Charmes” region outside Jezero Crater. The rover captured images of the formations on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), revealing pale, ghostly-looking rocks that stand out dramatically against the darker, dust-covered Martian landscape. Data from Perseverance's SuperCam instrument revealed that the rocks are rich in hydrated silica rather than being typical igneous rocks. That discovery has scientists particularly interested. On Earth, hydrated silica can form in environments involving hydrothermal activity or groundwater. These deposits are also capable of preserving microscopic fossils, making them valuable targets in the search for evidence of ancient life, according to another statement from NASA. NASA's Perseverance rover captured unusually bright, silica-rich rock in the "Idubi" area outside Jezero Crater on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), using its left Mastcam-Z camera. The pale formation stands out against the darker, dust-covered Martian terrain. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU) Perseverance is now conducting a closer investigation of the formations, using its instruments to gather detailed chemical and mineralogical data that could help scient

The thin, flattened formations resemble tiny potato chips. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Curiosity used its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), mounted on the end of its robotic arm, to capture detailed close-up images of the formations on Nov. 7 — the rover's 5,067th Martian day , or Sol 5067. Meanwhile, NASA's Perseverance rover has been investigating a collection of unusually bright rocks in an area called "Idubi," located in the “Lac de Charmes” region outside Jezero Crater. The rover captured images of the formations on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), revealing pale, ghostly-looking rocks that stand out dramatically against the darker, dust-covered Martian landscape. Data from Perseverance's SuperCam instrument revealed that the rocks are rich in hydrated silica rather than being typical igneous rocks. That discovery has scientists particularly interested. On Earth, hydrated silica can form in environments involving hydrothermal activity or groundwater. These deposits are also capable of preserving microscopic fossils, making them valuable targets in the search for evidence of ancient life, according to another statement from NASA. NASA's Perseverance rover captured unusually bright, silica-rich rock in the "Idubi" area outside Jezero Crater on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), using its left Mastcam-Z camera. The pale formation stands out against the darker, dust-covered Martian terrain. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU) Perseverance is now conducting a closer investigation of the formations, using its instruments to gather detailed chemical and mineralogical data that could help scientists determine how the rocks formed and whether they preserve potential signs of past microbial activity. NASA's Curiosity rover captured this view of distinctive polygon-shaped patterns outlined by raised ridges in the Martian bedrock using its Mast Camera (Mastcam) on Nov. 13, 2026 (Sol 5073). The unusual textures resemble formations the rover encountered earlier in its climb up Mount Sharp. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Back at Mount Sharp , Curiosity has also spotted another geological curiosity: the return of distinctive polygon-shaped patterns across the Martian bedrock. The rover's latest images, captured on Nov. 13, 2026 (Sol 5073), show small, regularly shaped polygons outlined by raised ridges, resembling patterns the rover encountered earlier in its climb up the layered mountain, whose rocky slopes preserve a record of Mars' changing climate and ancient watery environments. Scientists say these formations could have developed through several processes, including mineral shrinkage as water evaporated, temperature changes or the expansion and compaction of buried sediments, according to a statement from NASA. By studying the composition of the rocks and the material cementing the raised ridges around the polygons , researchers hope to determine which processes shaped the terrain. Together, these discoveries highlight how much Mars' seemingly barren landscape can reveal about its past. As Curiosity continues climbing Mount Sharp and Perseverance investigates ancient terrain beyond Jezero Crater , both rovers are helping piece together the planet's unique features and complex geological history.

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' gets final trailer, explaining why Steve Rogers is back and showing an epic battle with the X-Men
item.description: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just landed, and it finally puts the spotlight on our boy Steve Rogers. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. Previous trailers played it safe, mostly setting up the conflict and introducing Victor Von Doom. Now it’s time for one last explosive look at the film before it tries to conquer cinemas next month. Disney and Marvel Studios have just released a "final trailer" that puts the focus back on Steve Rogers — no longer Captain America but still ready to use Mjolnir — and Thor as the veterans leading the New Avengers, former colleagues, the Fantastic Four, and even Fox's X-Men (after some first-encounter fights, of course) against Doom and his followers. A few dodgy CG shots aside, it looks grand, and if you're a big X-Men fan, it's hard not to get goosebumps when Cyclops (James Marsden) finally gets to say the thing. The multiverse-spanning story is still largely kept a secret in this trailer, but at least we get a better sense of what the emotional stakes are for Rogers and how all these heroes can realistically work together against the greatest threat they've faced so far (even if most of them won't get more than a few lines). (Image credit: Marvel) As for Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, this isn't his trailer, but the mysterious Latverian witches — who have fueled many theories online for months — are finally seen in motion. Doom has, however, received a simple but evocative poster that mirrors one of the original Iron Man ones. Even though Marvel Studios' honcho, Kevin Feige, has shot down the theory that this Victor Von Doom is a Tony Stark variant , you can't stop marketing from doing the obvious things, it seems. We won't complain. (Image credit: Marvel Studios) Avengers: Doomsday won't fix all of the Multiverse Saga's shortcomings, but at the very least, it looks like a proper fun time with more toys being mashed together than ever before and proper stakes. Right before Christmas, it's hard to resist such a pitch. Avengers: Doomsday assembles on December 18, 2026, only in cinemas...Yes, it opens the same day as Dune: Part Three . item.title: The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026
item.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

item.title: Ghana’s Black Challenge Conquer the World With First-Ever Amputee Football World Cup Title
item.description: Pure joy on the pitch as Ghana’s Black Challenge mark their historic 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup triumph in Mexico. Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have officially conquered the world after edging Morocco 1–0 in the final of the 2026 World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF) World Cup in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico on Sunday, November 22, 2026. For anyone keeping an eye on international football and West African sporting milestones, this is a moment worth celebrating—it marks Ghana’s very first Amputee Football World Cup crown. The championship match brought together two African powerhouses and served as a high-stakes showdown between familiar rivals, following Ghana’s earlier continental triumphs against Morocco, including the 2024 African Amputee Cup of Nations final. Captain Richard Arthur Opentil stepped up as the decisive hero, scoring the lone goal in the 32nd minute. From there, Ghana dug deep with grit, smart positioning, and defensive discipline to shut out Morocco and bring the trophy home. Intense action between Morocco and Ghana during the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. What makes Ghana’s run in Mexico even more memorable is how much they had to overcome in the knockout stages. The Black Challenge defeated the United States 3–1 in the Round of 16, eased past Egypt 2–0 in the quarter-finals behind a brace from forward Mubarik Mohammed , and then edged a tense semi-final 1–1 after extra time before winning 4–3 on penalties. Individual brilliance shone right alongside the team trophy. Forward Mubarik Mohammed finished as the tournament’s top scorer with seven goals, earning the Golden Boot award. Back home, the achievement sparked widespread celebration, with congratulatory messages from Ghana’s leadership—including President John Dramani Mahama and the Ministry of Sports and Recreation—alongside financial backing and pledges from corporate supporters and philanthropists such as Gold Fields Ghana and Mohammed Raii through the EEZZY Group Foundation. Speaking after the victory, captain Richard Arthur Opentil dedicated the triumph to Ghana and its supporters as an early Christmas gift to the nation. Ghana’s Black Challenge celebrate lifting their maiden 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup trophy in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. If you are wondering what the WAFF Amputee Football World Cup is all about, it is the premier international championship for amputee football, governed globally by the World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF). Played according to rules adapted from FIFA’s Laws of the Game, amputee football is fast-paced, physically demanding, and thrilling to watch. Matches feature seven players per side—outfield players with lower-limb amputations playing on forearm crutches without prostheses, and goalkeepers with single-arm amputations—with crutches treated as part of the player’s body rather than a tool to intentionally play the ball. Goalkeeper Razak and the Black Challe

item.title: Esposito emulates Vieri with Inter hat-trick but De Ketelaere haunts him again
item.description: Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born. We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France . Continue reading...

item.title: I’m planning my first dark sky trip, and all because this educational star projector showed me what I’m missing
item.description: I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience. Perhaps I’d come away with a sense of wonder and delight, coupled with mild irritation at having to hunt down three AA batteries to power it. Instead, I was filled with envy as the Brainstorm Night Sky reminded me just what I was missing, thanks to the rigors of light pollution . A few minutes after powering it down, I was already making plans for my first dark sky trip, yearning for a view that rivaled the Brainstorm’s cosmic images. Brainstorm Night Sky Projector review Whatever your age, the Brainstorm Night Sky is so simple to use The Brainstorm Night Sky projector comes with four or six slides, depending on whether you buy the blue or gray version (Image credit: Chris McMullen) Draw the curtains, press the Night Sky’s single button (tilting the projector and twisting the focus as appropriate) and it projects a circular image onto a ceiling or wall. Press the button again and the projection slowly begins to rotate, slowly but stutter-free. It really is that simple to operate and, aimed at budding astronomers aged eight or above, it's reasonably lightweight without feeling flimsy. Depending on the model you buy, you’ll get four or six interchangeable slides. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) Specifications Weight: 14.8 oz (420 g) Bulb type: Non-specified Laser: No Control: On-unit Rotation: Yes, one speed Projection area: Up to 8.2 ft (2.5 m) Sleep timer: Yes (30 mins) Power: 3x AA batteries Speaker: No I was initially a little surprised by the size of the projection: at up to 8.2 feet (2.5 m) wide it’s not going to fill an entire ceiling. It also switches off after 30 minutes, a limit that can’t be disabled, so if you’re looking to put on your own space-themed party this is not the projector for you. But it’s on point for home education and, priced from $49.99, the Brainstorm Night Sky projector won’t break the bank. There’s minimal distortion around the edge of the images; the planets are spherical from the word go, unlike some projectors where I’ve had to tweak them to stop Mars turning into an egg. And I never once had to crane my neck because half the solar system had been projected onto a bookcase. This projector revealed what light pollution had taken from me There are two slides featuring the Northern Hemisphere’s starscape, with and without labelled constellations. But it’s on point for home education and, priced from $49.99, the Brainstorm Night Sky projector won’t break the bank. There’s minimal distortion around the edge of the images; the planets are spherical from the word go, unlike some projectors where I’ve had to tweak them to stop Mars turning into an egg. And I never once had to crane my neck because half the solar system had been projected onto a bookcase. This projector revealed what light pollution had taken from me There are two slides featuring the Northern Hemisphere’s starscape, with and without labelled constellations. Chris McMullen There are two slides featuring the Northern Hemisphere’s starscape, with and without labelled constellations. Chris McMullen There are two slides featuring the Northern Hemisphere’s starscape, with and without labelled constellations. Chris McMullen The Brainstorm Night Sky model I tested comes with four slides, each with a case to protect them from smudges and sticky fingers. You place one into the provided slide housing then insert that into the projector. There’s the moon, the solar system, and two showing the Northern Hemisphere’s night sky, as seen from Hawaii (a key location for astronomy). I can appreciate the educational value of the first couple, even if I am still seething at Pluto being demoted back in 2006. But it was the latter pair of slides that really opened my eyes to what I could be seeing over my head. I can spot maybe 10-20 stars from my backyard, cloud cover permitting; thanks to light pollution , that’s it. Even though the best stargazing apps can show me what I should see, when I step outside, all I typically see with the naked eye is the odd pinprick in the void. The Brainstorm Night Sky uses three AA batteries, but they’re not included with the projector. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) But as soon as I inserted that third slide, a striking stellar display appeared above my head, with more stars than I could hope to count. Even knowing that Hawaii’s night sky stretches far further than eight feet across, the difference between this view and the one from my house was like night and day. Brainstorm claims this slide features over 20,000 stars, though that’s likely referring to the source photo rather than the projected image. The fourth slide — the same crisp starscape but with every visible constellation labelled — was almost as attention-grabbing. Educational value aside, it drove home that I couldn’t see the majority of these star patterns to name them, my local night sky is that polluted. Knowing what I was missing out on made me determined to take my stargazing further afield. Some of the best smart telescopes can lessen the impact of light pollution, but stepping away from skyglow is the most effective option. Hawaii’s a little far to travel, but I’ve already started looking into local dark sky sites. I just need to grab a pair of the best binoculars for stargazing , hop on my bike and I’m ready to go. The Brainstorm Night Sky is a solid, budget-priced educational tool, but it has one drawback You can purchase one additional Southern Hemisphere slide, but beyond that you’re limited to the included slides. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) The Brainstorm Night Sky’s projections are crisp enough that you can easily make out every constellation name, but they could be a hair brighter. The Ainael Meter Galaxy Projector , for example, delivers more illumination. If you want to use the Brainstorm Night Sky to relax, the rotate function gives its projections an oddly hypnotic effect, and the device is whisper-quiet to boot. And while Brainstorm doesn’t specify battery life, one set of rechargeables lasted me for several days. Unfortunately, the Brainstorm Night Sky's slide collection is a little limited. There are two models, a blue version with four slides (the one I tested) and a gray version with six slides (featuring additional space shuttle and black hole images). The included instructions state you can purchase an additional slide disc showing the Southern Hemisphere’s stars, but that’s a maximum of seven images. Nor is this projector compatible with the slides from the Brainstorm Deep Sky Projector It’s a little disappointing given that Brainstorm has clearly put thought into the projector’s educational value. Those instructions double as a poster of the solar system, and children can use a “secret code” (printed on the instructions) to explore more astronomy facts on the company’s website. Offering extra slide packs, of the kind you can buy for the Pococo Galaxy Projector , would give it more long-term appeal. As is, I can see its novelty and educational value diminishing over time, at which point you can upgrade to one of the best star projectors . If you’re not bothered by the lack of expandability, the Brainstorm Night Sky’s price, image quality and ease of use still make it a useful tool for kindling a child’s interest in astronomy, or as a budget-friendly gift for junior stargazers. It’s certainly spurred me into action — how much is a plane ticket to Hawaii, anyway?

item.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
item.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. A model of one of the Phobos spacecraft on display in the Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics in Moscow, Russia. (Image credit: Музей Космонавтики from Россия, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons) To say that a lot hinged on the success of the mission would be an understatement, given the unfortunate fate of the probe's predecessor, Phobos 1, which went offline on Sept. 2, 1988, after a faulty command sequence was initiated while the spacecraft was on its way to Mars. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues. item.content:encoded:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. A model of one of the Phobos spacecraft on display in the Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics in Moscow, Russia. (Image credit: Музей Космонавтики from Россия, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons) To say that a lot hinged on the success of the mission would be an understatement, given the unfortunate fate of the probe's predecessor, Phobos 1, which went offline on Sept. 2, 1988, after a faulty command sequence was initiated while the spacecraft was on its way to Mars. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues. Over the course of the next several weeks, Phobos 2 was able to overcome some of these setbacks and successfully began sending useful scientific data about the Martian environment back to Earth. By March, all the probe's science instruments appeared to be functioning normally, and despite the earlier loss of one of its processors, the remaining two had continued to facilitate control of the spacecraft by its Soviet ground control team. An image of Phobos captured by the Soviet Union's Phobos 2 probe. (Image credit: Roscosmos) Unexplained failure That all changed on March 27, 1989, as Phobos 2 prepared to capture navigational images of its namesake as the Martian moon passed, which would be useful in advance of another forthcoming flyby in early April. Achieving this meant that the probe had to be angled in such a way that it faced Phobos, whereby its communications antennas would be temporarily directed away from Earth. During the imaging portion of the maneuver, all appeared to go smoothly, but soon afterward, ground controllers realized they were unable to reestablish contact with the probe. An image of Mars and its moon Phobos captured by the Soviet Union's Phobos 2 spacecraft on Feb. 28, 1989. Phobos 2 took a total of 13 color sets of images of Phobos before contact was lost on March 27, 1989. (Image credit: Roscosmos) A few fleeting radio contacts were made over the ensuing hours, which engineers believed might indicate that during the period of signal loss required for imagery of Phobos to be obtained, the spacecraft may have begun to spin uncontrollably. If this were the case, and the spacecraft could not reorient its solar panels toward the sun, it would eventually lose all power. No further contact with Phobos 2 could be established beyond this point, although images from the probe's final close encounter with the Martian moon were successfully delivered back to Soviet ground controllers. While investigators identified a failure involving the spacecraft's onboard computer system as the most probable explanation, to this day, the exact cause of the events leading to the loss remains unknown. Theories involving the failure Although questions remain about the fate of Phobos 2, several theories have been put forward over the years. According to authors Paolo Ulivi and David M. Harland , one of the simplest explanations was that the spacecraft was damaged after an impact with other material orbiting the Martian moon, although later modeling by Soviet engineers and American teams at NASA's Jet Propulsion Lab seemed to rule this out. The final image transmitted from the Soviet Union's Phobos 2 spacecraft shortly before losing communication with Earth. (Image credit: Roscosmos) A more likely scenario involved failure of the probe's second attitude control computer, which had already begun experiencing technical issues as Phobos 2 arrived in Martian orbit. With two of its three processors now offline, the third and sole remaining computer was unable to maintain control of the spacecraft on its own. An additional factor might have been power loss from battery drainage while the probe's solar arrays were directed away from the sun, and with no failsafe to power down any non-critical systems under such conditions, the spacecraft would likely have undergone significant power loss. However, the probe's failure was only one part of the mystery: equally perplexing had been the unusual images Phobos 2 captured in its final moments, which later sparked speculation — and conspiracy theories — about what might have been behind the spacecraft's sudden demise. The shadow in Phobos 2's final photos Soviet test pilot Marina Popovich. (Image credit: Keystone/Hulton Archive/Getty Images) In some of the final images captured by Phobos 2, an unusual, elongated shadow had been visible in the frame, which with time would begin to prompt the most unusual of all the theories about the probe's demise: that it had been disabled by an alien spacecraft. Among the proponents of this theory had been Marina Popovich, a former experimental pilot and the first Soviet woman to break the sound barrier, who set over 100 world aviation records in her career. In 1991, Popovich held a press conference at the Soviet Consulate in San Francisco, where she claimed a cigar-shaped object had been photographed near the Martian moon, which she believed to be an alien mothership . Given her storied background in Soviet aerospace history, Popovich's views likely carried a degree of credibility unlike most others. However, that did not make them accurate. Explaining the Phobos "shadow" Determining what the images actually show requires an understanding of the probe's orbit, particularly with relation to the Martian moon it was attempting to photograph. At the time, the spacecraft and Phobos were in almost the same orbit, and moving at very similar speeds. As Ulivi and Harland note , due to these conditions, the probe's Termoskan multispectral imager often captured images that "included the shadow of the moon on the planet's surface as a dark oblong cigar-shaped feature." In 1991, a NASA-led study of the Termoskan observations concluded that the unusual appearance of the shadow most likely resulted from a combination of factors acting together. The study team attributed these to the scanning instrument itself, as well as the spacecraft's near-co-orbital motion with Phobos, its viewing direction, and finally, a slight rocking motion the researchers concluded the spacecraft had likely exhibited at the time. item.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
item.description: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. Observations of the Welopō'ai triple-star system, located 28 light-years from Earth. The image on the left shows the two components of the system: Welopō'ai A, a closely orbiting red dwarf and white dwarf pair, and Welopō'ai B, a second white dwarf located much farther away. The image on the right provides a close-up view of the inner pair, revealing the faint white dwarf companion (Ab) detected using the Gemini North telescope's 'Alopeke instrument. The overlaid curves illustrate the stars'
item.dc:creator: Keith Cooper
item.content:encoded: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. Observations of the Welopō'ai triple-star system, located 28 light-years from Earth. The image on the left shows the two components of the system: Welopō'ai A, a closely orbiting red dwarf and white dwarf pair, and Welopō'ai B, a second white dwarf located much farther away. The image on the right provides a close-up view of the inner pair, revealing the faint white dwarf companion (Ab) detected using the Gemini North telescope's 'Alopeke instrument. The overlaid curves illustrate the stars' orbital paths. (Image credit: Photo : Pan-STARRS1/STScI/MAST (left); International Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab (right). Graphic compilation: Étienne Artigau and Heidi White (UdeM/IREx)) SPIRou discovers planets by measuring how much their gravity tugs on their host star. Think of a star and planet orbiting a kind of gravitational balancing point between them called a center of mass. This center of mass is usually inside the star, since the star is far more massive than the planet, but crucially not at its very center, so the star appears to wobble to and fro around the combined center of mass. The spectrometer measures this wobble in the form of a Doppler shift in the star's light that can be translated into the velocity at which the star is moving around this center of mass. Astronomers call this a 'radial velocity'. A large gas giant like Jupiter might incur a radial velocity of hundreds of meters per second, while an Earth-mass planet generates a radial velocity of tens of meters. Yet the object that SPIRou found orbiting close to the red dwarf was creating a huge radial velocity signals of 10 miles (16 kilometers) per second. Whatever it was, it was not a planet. With the help of the eight-meter Gemini North telescope on Hawaii's Mauna Kea, Artigau's team were able to identify the mystery object as a white dwarf. "The unusual combination of high mass and very low brightness left only one plausible explanation: it was the remnant of a dead star," said Charles-Antoine Parent, an undergraduate student at Université Laval and a co-author of the study. White dwarfs are not exactly rare, and even finding two white dwarfs together is not unheard of: WD 0727+482 is a binary white dwarf system 37 light-years away, for example. To encounter two white dwarfs in a triple system with a regular star though is a precious find. The reason being that the masses of white dwarfs are not generally well defined. Yet their masses are not random; they are directly connected to the mass of the star that produced them. Thanks to the newly discovered white dwarf being separated from the red dwarf by about 4.6 astronomical units (688 million kilometers/428 million miles) – that's closer than Jupiter orbits our sun – Artigau's team were able to measure their masses to within an uncertainty of less than 1%. They found that the red dwarf has a mass 42% that of our sun and the newly discovered white dwarf has a mass 62% that of our sun. When the white dwarf was a regular star it would have had a mass 40% greater than our sun. The second more distant white dwarf orbits the pair of them. The Gemini North telescope in Hawaii, which helped identify the stars in the Welopō'ai triple system. (Image credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/J. Warner) The Welopō'ai system is therefore a good system for testing our models of stellar evolution that dictate how massive a white dwarf should be. If we know the white dwarf's mass with high precision, scientists can also use that as a starting point from which to explore the extreme physics of the white dwarf's condensed matter, which is being held up and prevented from contracting any further by something called electron degeneracy pressure – the unwillingness of negatively charged electrons to crush down any further and merge with positively charged protons to form neutrons . That takes the extra gravity from a more massive star to form a neutron star . So why should Welopō'ai not exist? The trouble is that when stars turn into red giants they really stir things up. Even if the red giant didn't expand out as far as the red dwarf, the expansion should have destabilized the red dwarf's orbit and potentially even caused it to crash into the red giant. Yet here the red dwarf is in a happily stable orbit like nothing had happened. "That is the question driving our next observations," said Dufour. It is hoped that further, more detailed, measurements of the gravitational interactions between the three members of the Welopō'ai system will help the team disentangle the evolutionary history of the trio to better understand their orbits and how the red dwarf survived. And because they are so relatively close to us, we have the advantage of being able to make high-precision measurements. "Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises," said Artigau. "Even when we're searching for planets, our universe often has something completely unexpected waiting for us." The discovery of the Welopō'ai triple system is described in a paper published on Nov. 19 in Astronomy & Astrophysics .

item.title: From Mind Games to Ghost Stories! 5 Nollywood Titles to Stream This Week
item.description: Wande Thomas’s psychological thriller Spiraling, starring Toni Tones, Jim Iyke, Folu Storms and Seun Ajayi on KAVA, is among the titles recommended to watch this week. Wrongfully accused, caught in a web of lies, pulled into a dangerous family feud or haunted by a past you never saw coming. This week’s streaming picks have a little bit of everything for anyone who enjoys a story that refuses to let them relax. We’ve rounded up five titles across Circuits, Netflix, Prime Video and KAVA, taking you from psychological thrillers and gang conflicts to supernatural mysteries and a night out that spirals into something much bigger. Extra Mile — Circuits Sometimes trying to do a good deed for someone else is how everything goes sideways. That is the trap at the heart of this drama, where a woman ends up behind bars for a crime she never committed after stepping in to help a friend. Mercy Johnson – Okojie , Jim Iyke and Lilian Esoro carry the story forward under Kayode Kasum ‘s direction, working from a screenplay by Folasade Osibo and with Joy Grant – Ekong and Solate Ovundah – Akarolo on board as producers. Double Decoy — Circuits Moving from courtroom-style heartbreak straight into psychological mind games, our next pick on the same platform turns suspicion into a sport. Nothing looks straightforward when hidden agendas, shifting loyalties and high-stakes deception collide in this tense thriller. As every move feels like a test of trust, viewers are left guessing who is really pulling the strings, anchored by Kanayo O . Kanayo , Sola Sobowale and Gideon Okeke . Behind the scenes, the credits point to Oluwafemi Isaac Akinsipe alongside Nnamdi E . Odunze and Chichi Stylxz . The Covenant Season 2 — Netflix If that kind of high-stakes tension gets you in the mood for bigger battles and family rivalries, head over to Netflix next where the stakes climb even higher. Picking up right where the first run left off, the second season plunges deeper into power struggles, family loyalty and survival as Dagogo gets pulled further into dangerous conflicts and old scores. Gideon Okeke is back alongside Uzee Usman in a story created by Vincent Okonkwo and directed by Menelik Shabazz (“menelikfather”), mixing tense action, supernatural undertones and shifting alliances that keep the pressure on. Ajuwaya 2: Ghost of Selema — Prime Video Trading gang wars and big empires for eerie small-town secrets, our next stop on Prime Video shifts the tension somewhere much closer to home. Imagine posting up for youth service in a new town only to become the fixation of a troubled young man—and then digging into his past and finding a secret that links him straight to you with every reason to haunt you. Tolu LordTanner directs this suspenseful drama starring Godspower Nwogwugwu , Damilola Onitilo , Oyeyemi Adeoye and Ovy Godwin . item.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
item.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. Its guiding promise captures the thinking behind the business: “ With Saina Properties, you own with certainty.” Solape Fayemi is the Chief Executive Officer of Sa

item.content:encoded: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. Its guiding promise captures the thinking behind the business: “ With Saina Properties, you own with certainty.” Solape Fayemi is the Chief Executive Officer of Saina Properties , a real estate company operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States, and the United Arab Emirates. She leads the company’s vision and strategic direction, overseeing its work across property advisory and verification, sales and brokerage, and developments. Drawing on her experience in the investment industry, Solape brings a strong understanding of wealth creation, risk management, and capital preservation to her approach to real estate. Under her leadership, Saina Properties is focused on making property ownership a more informed and transparent experience, built on professional guidance, due diligence and long-term client relationships. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...
